nodes.summary: Vectorized sigmoid — writes sigmoid(x_i) into a caller-provided out buffer by zipping x.iter() with out.iter_mut() and reusing the scalar sigmoid primitive.

nodes.name: PersonalitySnapshot
nodes.summary: Const-generic committed snapshot of personality weights carrying the weight vector, ArchetypeLabel, BLAKE3 commitment, and version; impl provides commit/verify/to_bytes/from_bytes and from_composition/from_parts constructors.

nodes.name: from_composition
nodes.summary: Builds a PersonalitySnapshot from a live PersonalityWeightedComposition by extracting its weight vector and delegating to from_parts_with_commit.

nodes.name: from_parts
nodes.summary: Constructs a PersonalitySnapshot from explicit weight vector, archetype, blake3 commitment, and version — the roundtrip counterpart to to_bytes used for restore operations.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Computes the BLAKE3 hash of archetype bytes || each weight's little-endian bytes and stores it as the snapshot's commitment — excludes version so commits are idempotent across version bumps.

nodes.name: verify_blake3
nodes.summary: Recomputes the BLAKE3 commitment over the current weights+archetype and compares against the stored hash — tamper-detection gate used before restoring a snapshot.

nodes.name: to_bytes
nodes.summary: Serializes the snapshot to a fixed-layout Vec<u8>: 16-byte archetype || N*4-byte little-endian f32 weights || 32-byte blake3 || 8-byte little-endian u64 version.

nodes.name: from_bytes
nodes.summary: Deserializes a PersonalitySnapshot from a byte buffer, validating length and parsing archetype/weights/blake3/version fields with little-endian decoding — returns None on malformed input.

nodes.name: LayerDirectionSource
nodes.summary: Trait that any latent-direction layer must implement to participate in composition — exposes direction (the static d_i vector), recent_direction (drift signal), and belief_confidence (per-layer decay multiplier).

nodes.name: PersonalityConfig
nodes.summary: Hyperparameter struct for the personality kernel — tau (sigmoid temperature), alpha (drift learning rate), w_max (clamp bound), ema_decay (expected-reward smoothing); provides Default and is_valid sanity check.

nodes.name: ArchetypeLabel
nodes.summary: 16-byte blake3-derived identity newtype wrapping [u8; 16] — constructed deterministically from a string via from_str (blake3-truncated) and used as the per-entity archetype tag carried in PersonalitySnapshot commitments.

nodes.name: is_valid
nodes.summary: Sanity check on PersonalityConfig — verifies tau, alpha, w_max, and ema_decay are all finite (non-NaN, non-infinity) before the kernel uses them.

nodes.name: from_str
nodes.summary: Deterministically constructs an ArchetypeLabel from a string by computing blake3(s) and copying the first 16 bytes into the newtype — same input always yields the same label.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for katgpt-proof-cert: declares private modules and re-exports the public proof-certificate API surface, with the wasm witness subset gated behind the `wasm_proof_witness` feature flag.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` to conditionally compile the witness module and its re-exports; `#![allow(unexpected_cfgs)]` tolerates pass-through aggregate features like `full`.

nodes.name: certificate.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the core proof-certificate domain types: the `ProofCertificate` struct plus the `ProofProperty`, `ProofResult`, and `ProofEvidence` enums, together with constructors (`new`, `with_timestamp`, `passed`) and a `now_epoch_secs` timestamp helper.
nodes.languageNotes: Idiomatic Rust newtype-less struct with `impl` constructors; enums carry variant payloads (e.g. `ProofResult::Conditional { value, threshold, conditions }`).

nodes.name: chain.rs
nodes.summary: Topological proof-chain verifier: `verify_proof_chain` checks each certificate's prerequisites and implications against already-proven ids, while `topological_sort` performs Kahn's algorithm over the prerequisite DAG to produce a consistent evaluation order.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-rolled Kahn's algorithm using `VecDeque` and an adjacency list; operates over certificate id strings with a `HashMap<&str, usize>` index.

nodes.name: macros.rs
nodes.summary: Declares the `conditional_proof!` declarative macro (exported at crate root via `#[macro_export]`) that builds a `ProofCertificate` with a `Conditional` result, threshold, conditions, and implied proof ids.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `$crate::` path prefix so the macro resolves correctly when re-exported from downstream crates.

nodes.name: serde_impls.rs
nodes.summary: BLAKE3-integrity-checked binary persistence for certificate bundles: `save_certificates` writes a magic+version+length+postcard payload with a trailing blake3 checksum, `load_certificates` validates and deserializes it then runs `verify_proof_chain`, and `verify_checksum` standalone-verifies a file.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom binary framing (magic bytes, little-endian u32 length header) layered over `postcard` serde; relies on `blake3::hash` for tamper detection.

nodes.name: wasm_certificates.rs
nodes.summary: Produces the validator proof bundle via `generate_wasm_validator_certificates`, emitting P1-P4 certificates that attest deterministic correctness, native-vs-wasm equivalence, real-time feasibility, and LoRA win-rate delta from comparison/latency/mismatch inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Single large builder function that constructs multiple `ProofCertificate` instances inline; evidence payloads encoded with `postcard::to_allocvec`.

nodes.name: wasm_proof_witness.rs
nodes.summary: Witness-attested proof generation: the `WasmProofWitness` struct hashes (blake3) input + rules + validation result to produce a tamper-evident witness, convertible via `to_certificate` into a `ProofCertificate`, plus `generate_wasm_witness_certificates` which assembles the full P1-P5 witness-attested validator bundle.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `blake3::Hasher` with ordered `update` calls for domain-separated witness hashing; the `P5Derived` struct captures cross-certificate derivation provenance.

nodes.name: ProofCertificate
nodes.summary: Core serializable proof certificate struct carrying id, property, result, prerequisite/implies dependency lists, explanation, evidence payload, and a unix-epoch timestamp.

nodes.name: ProofProperty
nodes.summary: Enum classifying what a proof attests: SpatialConsistency, DeterministicCorrectness, RealtimeFeasibility, Convergence, or a Custom property.

nodes.name: ProofResult
nodes.summary: Enum representing proof outcome severity: Full (proven), Conditional (threshold-gated with value/threshold/conditions), Partial, or Failed.

nodes.name: ProofEvidence
nodes.summary: Enum attaching machine-checkable evidence to a proof: Benchmark metrics, Deterministic traces, Comparison against a reference, or a Custom binary payload.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a `ProofCertificate` with empty prerequisite/implies lists and a timestamp captured via `with_timestamp` + `now_epoch_secs`.

nodes.name: with_timestamp
nodes.summary: Constructs a `ProofCertificate` from an explicit caller-supplied timestamp, initializing the dependency lists and explanation to empty defaults.

nodes.name: passed
nodes.summary: Returns true when this certificate's result indicates a `Full` proof outcome.

nodes.name: ProofChainResult
nodes.summary: Result struct aggregating the outcome of `verify_proof_chain`: separate vectors of proven, conditional, and failed certificate ids.

nodes.name: verify_proof_chain
nodes.summary: Topologically sorts (via `topological_sort`) then walks a certificate list, classifying each as proven, conditional, or failed based on whether its prerequisites and implied ids are already in the proven set.

nodes.name: topological_sort
nodes.summary: Kahn's-algorithm topological sort over the certificate prerequisite DAG, returning a reordered vector plus the original indices so callers can correlate back to input positions.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds an explicit adjacency list + in-degree vector, drains a `VecDeque` queue of zero-in-degree nodes, and falls back to pushing cycles in input order.

nodes.name: save_certificates
nodes.summary: Serializes a certificate slice with `postcard`, prepends a magic + version + u32 length header, appends a trailing blake3 checksum, and writes the framed blob atomically to disk.

nodes.name: load_certificates
nodes.summary: Reads and validates a certificate file: checks size, magic bytes, version, and length header, deserializes the postcard payload, then runs `verify_proof_chain` to confirm dependency consistency before returning the slice.

nodes.name: verify_checksum
nodes.summary: Standalone integrity check: reads a file and recomputes its blake3 hash for comparison against an expected digest.

nodes.name: generate_wasm_validator_certificates
nodes.summary: Assembles the four-part validator proof bundle (P1 spatial/deterministic correctness, P2 native-vs-wasm equivalence, P3 real-time feasibility, P4 LoRA win-rate delta) from comparison, mismatch, latency, and lora-delta inputs.

nodes.name: WasmProofWitness
nodes.summary: Tamper-evident witness struct produced by blake3-hashing the input bytes, rules, and validation result, carrying the witness hash, optional violated rule, validation outcome, and input hash.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Primary `WasmProofWitness` constructor: hashes the input with blake3, then runs an ordered `Hasher::update` sequence over rules + validation result + violated rule to derive the witness hash.
nodes.languageNotes: Domain-separated hashing via ordered `blake3::Hasher::update` calls ensures distinct witnesses for semantically distinct inputs.

nodes.name: pass
nodes.summary: Convenience constructor delegating to `new` with a Pass validation result and no violated rule.

nodes.name: fail
nodes.summary: Convenience constructor delegating to `new` with a Fail validation result and the supplied violated rule string.

nodes.name: to_certificate
nodes.summary: Promotes a witness into a `ProofCertificate` by packing the witness hash, input hash, rules, and violated rule into a Custom evidence buffer and attaching a domain-tagged explanation.

nodes.name: generate_wasm_witness_certificates
nodes.summary: Assembles the full P1-P5 witness-attested validator bundle (deterministic correctness, native-vs-wasm equivalence, real-time feasibility with witness attestation, and LoRA win-rate delta), embedding `WasmProofWitness` hashes into each certificate's evidence and recording P5 derivation provenance via `P5Derived`.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for the Analytic Lattice — defines the core LatticeVector<N> and TransportOperator types and re-exports the four pure-math primitives (compose_chain, batch_compose_chain, direction_vector_decode, spectral_audit). Enforces the katgpt-core leaf discipline by keeping GpuFuture imports out.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses const-generic N on LatticeVector<N> with #[repr(transparent)] so the wrapper is ABI-identical to [f32; N] for SIMD kernels.

nodes.name: asoc.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the generic ASOC (Asymmetric Speculative Operator Cascade) trait shapes — PlasmaDraft, RederiveOp, and the ComposerCtx cache key — that riir-engine fills in with its GpuFuture impls. Holds no GpuFuture bound at the trait level to preserve the 5-repo commercial boundary.

nodes.name: audit.rs
nodes.summary: Spectral audit verifier (Plan 330 G6 gate) — computes a numerical-Jacobian tangent of a TransportOperator, projects it onto a DCT-II basis, and reports per-mode gains plus a spurious-coupling ratio used by the warm-tier reflection cycle to flag bad composites after the fact.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-software DCT-II projection (no FFT dependency); keeps the basis unnormalized because the normalization cancels in the spurious-ratio quotient.

nodes.name: batch_chain.rs
nodes.summary: Zone-batched chain composer that factors the shared boss/quest prefix once and applies each per-player suffix, turning O(N·k^3) naive per-player work into O((N+1)·k^3) to satisfy the G4 gate target.

nodes.name: chain.rs
nodes.summary: Core k×k transport operator chain composer with a zero-alloc scratch-buffer variant (compose_chain_into) for ASOC's hot path. Caps chain length at 16 to keep the G3 associativity gate (Frobenius error ≤ 1e-5) satisfiable.

nodes.name: decoder.rs
nodes.summary: SIMD direction-vector decoder that projects a LatticeVector state onto a direction and applies fast_sigmoid (NOT softmax, per AGENTS.md) to produce an action score in (0,1). Bit-identical across runs and fully stack-local.

nodes.name: LatticeVector
nodes.summary: Const-generic per-slot lattice vector wrapping [f32; N]. Slot-agnostic — the eggshell default is k=8 but any N compiles. #[repr(transparent)] makes it ABI-compatible with a raw slice for SIMD kernels.

nodes.name: TransportOperator
nodes.summary: Row-major k×k transport operator — the core matrix type that compose_chain multiplies and spectral_audit verifies. Provides validated constructors (from_row_major), identity/zeros factories, and a frobenius_norm diagnostic.

nodes.name: PlasmaDraft
nodes.summary: Object-safe trait for the plasma-tier (synchronous, stale-fallback) draft action. The impl MUST be deterministic in (self, ctx) — that determinism is what makes the stale fallback safe in the ASOC bot loop.

nodes.name: RederiveOp
nodes.summary: Object-safe trait for the hot-tier transport-operator rederive. Returns an associated future type Fut with NO GpuFuture bound at the trait level — riir-engine applies the GpuFuture<Output = TransportOperator> bound at the impl site to keep katgpt-core leaf-clean.
nodes.languageNotes: Associated type Fut has no bound here — the bound is added at the impl site in a different crate to avoid inverting the dependency graph.

nodes.name: ComposerCtx
nodes.summary: Per-tick composer context carrying only generic cache-keying fields (tick, zone_hash). Copy + Hash so the warm-tier reflection queue can clone it cheaply on every divergence event. Holds no game-IP state.

nodes.name: AuditReport
nodes.summary: Result of spectral_audit — per-mode DCT-II gains, the full mode-projection matrix, and a scalar spurious_ratio. passes_g6() returns true when spurious_ratio ≤ 5% threshold.

nodes.name: spectral_audit_with_modes
nodes.summary: Full spectral audit entry point — builds the numerical-Jacobian tangent via compute_tangent, projects it onto the DCT-II basis, and assembles the AuditReport with diagonal vs off-diagonal mode mass.

nodes.name: batch_compose_chain
nodes.summary: Typed zone-batched compose — validates prefix/suffix shapes, computes the prefix composite once via compose_chain_into, then runs each per-player suffix against it. Returns one TransportOperator per suffix in the caller-provided out buffer.

nodes.name: batch_compose_chain_into
nodes.summary: Zero-alloc raw-slice variant of batch_compose_chain for ASOC's hot path when a zone has N>1 players. Drives matmul_row_major_raw directly to avoid any typed-operator overhead in the inner loop.

nodes.name: ChainError
nodes.summary: Error enum for compose_chain — ChainLengthInvalid (empty or > MAX_CHAIN_LEN=16), DimensionMismatchK (operators disagree on k), DimensionMismatch, and DimensionOverflow (k^2 would overflow usize). Implements Display.

nodes.name: compose_chain
nodes.summary: Convenience chain compose — validates, allocates the result operator and a scratch buffer, then delegates to compose_chain_into. Use the _into variant on the hot path.

nodes.name: compose_chain_into
nodes.summary: Zero-alloc chain product — writes the result into a caller-provided TransportOperator and reuses a caller-provided scratch buffer. The hot-path primitive that ASOC's ComposerTick::poll calls per tick.

nodes.name: direction_vector_decode
nodes.summary: Primary scalar decoder — out = sigmoid((dot(state, direction) / N) * temperature). Const-generic N lets the compiler unroll the dot product and elide slice bounds checks on the hot path.

nodes.name: direction_vector_decode_into
nodes.summary: Batched decoder — iterates a slice of direction vectors and writes one sigmoid score per direction into a caller-provided out slice. The zero-alloc variant used by the HLA 5-scalar bridge.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel for the ICT (distributional branching-point detector) framework, re-exporting math primitives, branching selectors, the BranchingDetector runtime, BranchingReport output struct, and the Bebop H1->H2 acceptance upgrade. Gated behind the non-default `ict_branching` feature flag.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust module root with `pub mod` declarations plus `pub use` convenience re-exports at the module top level; entire module is behind a feature gate per Plan 294.

nodes.name: bebop_upgrade.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `AcceptanceForecastH2`, a Bebop-style upgrade that observes next-token logits and forecasts speculative-decoding acceptance length using the H2 (Renyi-2) entropy proxy with optional EMA smoothing and an adaptive gamma schedule.
nodes.languageNotes: Scratch-buffer `observe_and_forecast_into` variant avoids per-step allocation; SIMD-friendly unrolled softmax ladder over 4 logit lanes.

nodes.name: branching.rs
nodes.summary: Provides the ICT critical-branching predicate and the top-k% branching-point mask selector over uniqueness scores, with both percentile-based and absolute-threshold mask variants plus a reusable `_into` form that writes into a caller-supplied mask buffer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `sort_unstable_by` with `total_cmp` for deterministic f32 tie-breaking before threshold selection.

nodes.name: detector.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `BranchingDetector`, the inference-time runtime structure that consumes K candidate trajectories and emits a branching mask, per-step collision purity beta, and JS-divergence-based uniqueness scores via preallocated scratch buffers with optional EMA smoothing.
nodes.languageNotes: Preallocates six scratch buffers in `new` to keep the hot path allocation-free; `observe_and_detect_into` accepts a reusable `BranchingReport`.

nodes.name: math.rs
nodes.summary: Information-theory math primitives for the ICT module: collision purity (Renyi-2 collision probability), Renyi H2 entropy, Shannon H1 entropy, plus scalar and batched Jensen-Shannon divergence with caller-managed scratch buffers.
nodes.languageNotes: `collision_purity` delegates to a `simd_dot_f32` helper; JS divergence is clamped to a non-negative lower bound to absorb f32 rounding near identical distributions.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Defines `BranchingReport`, the output struct produced by `BranchingDetector`, carrying the boolean branching mask, per-step beta values, and uniqueness scores with convenience accessors for branching count and fraction.

nodes.name: AcceptanceForecastH2
nodes.summary: Stateful forecaster that upgrades Bebop's H1 acceptance-length estimate to an H2 (Renyi-2) variant by observing next-token logits, computing collision-purity-based forecasts, and exposing an adaptive gamma schedule with optional EMA smoothing of beta and alpha.

nodes.name: BranchingDetector
nodes.summary: Allocation-conscious runtime detector that ingests K candidate trajectories per step and produces a branching mask, per-step collision-purity beta, and JS-uniqueness scores, fusing the `branching` and `math` primitives with EMA tracking and reusable scratch buffers.

nodes.name: BranchingReport
nodes.summary: Output struct aggregating the branching mask, per-step beta, and uniqueness scores emitted by `BranchingDetector`, with helpers to compute total branching count and branching fraction.

nodes.name: observe_and_forecast
nodes.summary: Public entry point that validates next-token logits and delegates to `observe_and_forecast_into` with an internal scratch buffer.

nodes.name: observe_and_forecast_into
nodes.summary: Core forecast routine that softmaxes the next 4 logit lanes into a caller-supplied scratch buffer, computes collision purity, and updates EMA-smoothed beta/alpha to emit an H2 acceptance-length forecast.

nodes.name: adaptive_gamma
nodes.summary: Computes a clamped speculative-decoding gamma in `[gamma_min, gamma_max]` from the forecast acceptance length so the drafter budget tracks observed agreement.

nodes.name: branching_point_mask
nodes.summary: Selects the top-k% uniqueness-score positions as branching points by sorting a copy of the scores and dispatching to `branching_point_mask_into` with the derived threshold; falls back to a no-op on length mismatch.

nodes.name: branching_point_mask_into
nodes.summary: Writes a boolean branching-point mask into a caller-supplied buffer by flagging every position whose uniqueness score meets the absolute threshold; no-op on length mismatch.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a `BranchingDetector` with K-trajectory/action-dimension/k-percent/eta configuration and preallocates all scratch buffers (p_avg, m, u, mask, sorted) sized to the trajectory length for allocation-free hot-path operation.

nodes.name: observe_and_detect_into
nodes.summary: Hot-path detection routine that computes per-step mean trajectory, population collision-purity beta, per-trajectory JS divergence against the mean, sorts uniqueness scores, derives the top-k% branching mask via `branching_point_mask_into`, updates EMA state, and writes everything into a reusable `BranchingReport`.

nodes.name: collision_purity
nodes.summary: Computes the Renyi-2 collision probability (sum of squared probabilities) of a discrete distribution via a SIMD-accelerated dot product; the core beta primitive used across the ICT module.

nodes.name: shannon_h1
nodes.summary: Computes the Shannon H1 entropy of a probability slice, guarding against zero-probability inputs to keep the logarithm finite.

nodes.name: js_divergence
nodes.summary: Computes the symmetric Jensen-Shannon divergence between two discrete distributions p and q using a caller-supplied scratch buffer for the midpoint mixture, with the result clamped to absorb f32 rounding noise near zero.

nodes.name: js_divergence_batch
nodes.summary: Batched Jensen-Shannon divergence that, given a slice of distributions and the population mean, computes each distribution's divergence from the mean in a single allocation-free pass reusing a shared scratch mixture buffer.

nodes.name: compose.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the ComposeOp enum (And/Or) and the compose() helper that combines two PrunerExpr trees under the operadic composition then canonicalizes the result via the lattice word problem.
nodes.languageNotes: Dualizes the operadic composition on cubes to AND/OR composition of pruner constraints (Plan 252 Phase 2, Research 220).

nodes.name: composed_pruner.rs
nodes.summary: Implements ComposedPruner, a ConstraintPruner that evaluates a canonical AND/OR expression over a vector of child pruners, with both per-token and batched validity checks plus an extensive correctness and benchmark suite.
nodes.languageNotes: Batch path short-circuits via early-exit on Reject to beat per-token evaluation; tests include four/six-pruner speedup benchmarks with std::hint::black_box.

nodes.name: expr.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the PrunerResult (Accept/Reject/Unknown) and PrunerExpr (Atom/And/Or) AST types with constructors and a recursive evaluator that folds per-atom boolean vectors into a single result.
nodes.languageNotes: PrunerExpr uses Box children for infinite-depth recursive AST; eval implements three-valued logic where Unknown propagates conservatively.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel for the lattice_operad subsystem, re-exporting ComposeOp, compose, ComposedPruner, PrunerExpr, PrunerResult, and canonicalize as the public surface.

nodes.name: word_problem.rs
nodes.summary: Solves the distributive-lattice word problem for PrunerExpr by converting to disjunctive normal form, deduplicating and removing subsumed clauses, then rebuilding a canonical expression that is observably equal under three-valued evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: DNF is represented as Vec<Vec<atom_id>>; simplification applies idempotency, distributivity, and absorption laws by subsumption checks (is_subset).

nodes.name: vocab_channel_pruner.rs
nodes.summary: ROTATE-derived ConstraintPruner (Plan 228) that decomposes MLP output weights into kurtosis-maximizing vocabulary channels at load time and uses the resulting per-neuron token reachability maps to reject unreachable tokens during speculative decoding.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements ConstraintPruner trait from katgpt_core; uses AtomicUsize + RwLock for thread-safe active-context tracking and a binary little-endian serialization format with hash-stamped cache header.

nodes.name: compose
nodes.summary: Combines two PrunerExpr trees with the given ComposeOp (And/Or), then returns the canonicalized form produced by the word-problem solver.

nodes.name: ComposedPruner
nodes.summary: Composes multiple child ConstraintPruners under a canonical AND/OR PrunerExpr, dispatching per-token and batch validity queries by evaluating the expression against per-pruner results.

nodes.name: batch_is_valid
nodes.summary: Bulk-validates a candidate token slice by querying each child pruner in batch mode, then folding the per-pruner vectors through the composed PrunerExpr with early-exit semantics.

nodes.name: PrunerExpr
nodes.summary: Recursive AND/OR/Atom AST for pruner composition, with constructors (atom, and, or) and traversal methods (eval, atom_ids, node_count) used by the canonicalizer and evaluator.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Recursively evaluates the PrunerExpr against a per-atom-id slice of PrunerResults, implementing three-valued logic where And requires both Accept and Or requires either Accept while Unknown propagates conservatively.

nodes.name: canonicalize
nodes.summary: Top-level entry to the word-problem solver: converts a PrunerExpr to DNF, simplifies it under the absorption/distributivity laws, and rebuilds an equivalent canonical PrunerExpr.

nodes.name: to_dnf
nodes.summary: Recursively transforms a PrunerExpr into disjunctive normal form as a vector of clauses, distributing And over Or and concatenating clause vectors.

nodes.name: simplify_dnf
nodes.summary: Normalizes each DNF clause (sort + dedup), drops empty clauses, then removes any clause that is a strict superset of another (absorption law), yielding the minimal equivalent DNF.

nodes.name: is_subset
nodes.summary: Two-pointer test determining whether one sorted, deduplicated atom-id clause is a subset of another, used by simplify_dnf to detect absorption.

nodes.name: dnf_to_expr
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a PrunerExpr from simplified DNF by reducing each clause's atoms under PrunerExpr::and and then joining clauses under PrunerExpr::or.

nodes.name: skewness
nodes.summary: Computes the population skewness (gamma_1) of an f32 slice in a single O(n) pass, returning 0.0 for degenerate inputs without allocating.

nodes.name: excess_kurtosis
nodes.summary: Computes excess kurtosis (gamma_2 - 3) of an f32 slice in one pass; this is the kurtosis-maximization objective used by the ROTATE channel discovery loop.

nodes.name: householder_apply
nodes.summary: Applies the Householder reflection x -> x - 2*(h dot x)*h to a vector, the core linear-algebra primitive used to rotate neuron weight directions during channel discovery.

nodes.name: vocab_project
nodes.summary: Projects a neuron direction onto the vocabulary via the lm_head matrix to obtain per-token logits, used to discover which tokens a channel reaches.

nodes.name: iterative_token_mask
nodes.summary: Computes a boolean mask over logits using a z-score threshold (k_sigma * std around the mean), turning the projected vocab distribution into a set of active tokens for a channel.

nodes.name: topk_indices
nodes.summary: Returns the indices of the top-k largest f32 values using a sorted-insert sweep, used to pick the representative top_tokens for each discovered VocabChannel.

nodes.name: decompose_neuron
nodes.summary: Iteratively discovers up to max_channels VocabChannels for a single neuron weight by repeatedly rotating the residual direction and extracting masked token sets.

nodes.name: discover_channel
nodes.summary: Performs one round of channel discovery: optimizes a Householder reflection on a random initial direction, projects to vocab, masks via z-score, and returns the resulting VocabChannel with its moments and top tokens.

nodes.name: optimize_householder
nodes.summary: Coordinate-ascent optimizer that perturbs a Householder reflector to maximize excess kurtosis of the masked vocab projection, using finite differences and cosine-similarity acceptance.

nodes.name: decompose_layer_channels
nodes.summary: Decomposes every neuron in one MLP layer into vocab channels and aggregates their top-token sets into the per-neuron reachability vectors stored in VocabChannelMap.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Serializes VocabChannelMap to a compact little-endian binary layout (layer count, neuron count, token count, tokens) suitable for cached disk storage.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Parses the binary layout produced by serialize back into a VocabChannelMap, validating offsets and returning descriptive errors on truncated input.

nodes.name: decompose_model_channels
nodes.summary: Top-level driver that walks every layer of a TransformerWeights model, decomposes its MLP output neurons into vocab channels, and packages the result with timing and a weight hash for cache identity.

nodes.name: load_cached_pruner
nodes.summary: Reads and validates a cached pruner file by checking its CacheHeader (weight hash, vocab size, layer count) before deserializing the VocabChannelMap to skip recomputation.

nodes.name: save_pruner_cache
nodes.summary: Persists a VocabChannelPruner to disk as a binary cache file prefixed with a CacheHeader carrying the weight hash and shape metadata for future cache hits.

nodes.name: VocabChannelDecomposer
nodes.summary: Stateful driver for the ROTATE decomposition: holds a VocabChannelConfig and exposes decompose_neuron / discover_channel / optimize_householder to extract kurtosis-maximizing channels from neuron weights.

nodes.name: VocabChannelMap
nodes.summary: Per-layer, per-neuron sorted token reachability store with binary-search membership queries, layer/global unions, and little-endian serialize/deserialize for cached storage.

nodes.name: VocabChannelPruner
nodes.summary: Thread-safe ConstraintPruner implementation backed by a VocabChannelMap, using an AtomicUsize active layer and RwLock-protected neuron set to answer per-token and batch reachability queries during speculative decoding.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AtomicUsize + RwLock to satisfy ConstraintPruner's Sync requirement without copying the reachability map on context switches.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel for the mechanistic data attribution subsystem (Plan 111, Research 009), feature-gated behind `mech_attribution`. Declares the four core submodules and re-exports the public API: catalyst detection, template extraction, influence proxy scoring, and ROPD-rubric integration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `#[cfg(feature = "...")]` on both `mod` declarations and `pub use` re-exports, with `integration` additionally gated on `ropd_rubric`.

nodes.name: augmentation.rs
nodes.summary: Synthetic-sample augmentation: extracts reusable CatalystTemplates from sample groups and generates random variations of XML, code, LaTeX, database-row, and pure-repetition patterns for influence-proxy training.

nodes.name: catalyst.rs
nodes.summary: Core catalyst-pattern detection: scores input text across five structural pattern classes (XML tags, code identifiers, LaTeX formulas, database rows, pure repetition) and returns the dominant pattern above a confidence threshold.

nodes.name: integration.rs
nodes.summary: ROPD rubric integration: blends a rubric score with a catalyst influence score via a clamped weighted combination, with a 50% boost applied to high-influence catalyst samples. Provides both single-sample and batch entry points.
nodes.languageNotes: Conditionally compiled only when both `mech_attribution` and `ropd_rubric` features are enabled.

nodes.name: scoring.rs
nodes.summary: Activation influence proxy: stores catalyst-pattern activation vectors, scores incoming activations by max cosine similarity to stored patterns, and ranks a batch of samples by combined catalyst overlap (using a blake3-derived deterministic activation proxy).
nodes.languageNotes: Derives a deterministic 8-dim f32 activation vector from `blake3` hashes of sample text as a modelless stand-in for real activations.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Core data types for the mech_attribution subsystem: `MechInfluenceScore` (overlap + high-influence flag), `CatalystPattern` enum with Display impl, and `InfluenceConfig` with sensible defaults.

nodes.name: extract_template
nodes.summary: Groups samples by detected catalyst pattern and dispatches each group to the matching per-pattern template extractor, returning a vec of CatalystTemplates.

nodes.name: generate_synthetic
nodes.summary: Generates N synthetic sample variations from a CatalystTemplate by dispatching to the matching per-pattern variation generator and filling placeholders with random tokens.

nodes.name: extract_xml_template
nodes.summary: Walks the byte stream of the first sample to extract an XML skeleton template with `{}` placeholders for tag-internal text content.

nodes.name: extract_code_template
nodes.summary: Scans character boundaries to replace alphanumeric identifier runs in a code sample with `{}` placeholders, preserving punctuation structure.

nodes.name: extract_latex_template
nodes.summary: Converts a LaTeX formula sample into a template by abstracting command arguments and superscript/subscript bodies into placeholders.

nodes.name: extract_db_template
nodes.summary: Detects the delimiter of the first non-empty line (CSV/TSV/etc.) and emits a same-width placeholder row as the database-row template.

nodes.name: extract_repetition_template
nodes.summary: Returns the first sample verbatim as a repetition template when the sample is dominated by a small number of repeated whitespace-delimited tokens.

nodes.name: CatalystTemplate
nodes.summary: Data carrier bundling a detected CatalystPattern with its extracted template string and the list of variable TemplateFields.

nodes.name: detect_catalyst_pattern
nodes.summary: Public convenience wrapper that calls detect_catalyst_pattern_with_threshold with the default threshold.

nodes.name: detect_catalyst_pattern_with_threshold
nodes.summary: Scores the input against all five pattern classes and returns the highest-scoring CatalystPattern provided its score clears the supplied threshold, else None.

nodes.name: catalyst_score
nodes.summary: Builds a MechInfluenceScore for the input text by running threshold-based pattern detection and marking high-influence when the overlap exceeds the configured catalyst threshold.

nodes.name: xml_score
nodes.summary: Scores XML-ness of the text by counting `<tag>` open/close density relative to text length.

nodes.name: code_score
nodes.summary: Scores code-ness by measuring the density of symbol punctuation (braces, semicolons, operators) and identifier-like tokens in the character stream.

nodes.name: latex_score
nodes.summary: Scores LaTeX-ness by counting backslash-command prefixes (especially before alphabetic characters) and math delimiters as a density over text length.

nodes.name: database_score
nodes.summary: Scores database-row-ness by checking that multiple non-empty lines share a consistent field count when split on a detected delimiter (CSV/TSV/etc.).

nodes.name: pure_repetition_score
nodes.summary: Scores pure-repetition-ness by searching for the shortest substring whose tiled repetition covers most of the input, returning the coverage ratio.

nodes.name: score_with_influence
nodes.summary: Blends a rubric score with a catalyst influence score using a clamped weighted combination, applying a 50% boost to the catalyst component when the sample is flagged high-influence.

nodes.name: batch_score_with_influence
nodes.summary: Vectorized wrapper around score_with_influence that applies the blending to a parallel slice of rubric and catalyst scores, returning original-index/score pairs.

nodes.name: ActivationInfluenceProxy
nodes.summary: In-memory store of recorded catalyst activation vectors that exposes construction, recording (weighted by outcome quality), influence scoring via cosine similarity, and a stored-count accessor.

nodes.name: record_catalyst_activation
nodes.summary: Stores a catalyst activation vector, replicating it a clamped number of times proportional to the outcome quality so high-quality examples exert more influence.

nodes.name: influence_score
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum cosine similarity between the query activation vector and any stored catalyst pattern, or 0.0 if the store is empty.

nodes.name: cosine_similarity
nodes.summary: Computes the cosine similarity between two f32 slices using dot product over L2 norm products.

nodes.name: batch_influence_rank
nodes.summary: Ranks a batch of text samples by combined catalyst overlap (70% catalyst_score + 30% activation similarity from a blake3-derived proxy), sorts descending, marks the top-k as high-influence, and returns the ranked list.

nodes.name: MechInfluenceScore
nodes.summary: Result struct for mechanistic influence scoring: holds the catalyst overlap magnitude, the detected CatalystPattern, and a boolean flag for high-influence samples.

nodes.name: CatalystPattern
nodes.summary: Enum of the five supported catalyst pattern classes (XmlRepetition, CodeSignature, LatexFormula, DatabaseRow, PureRepetition) plus a None variant, with a human-readable Display implementation.

nodes.name: InfluenceConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration struct for influence scoring: top_k_fraction for batch ranking, catalyst_threshold for high-influence flagging, and min_repetition_length for repetition detection. Provides a Default with conservative values.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel for the Posterior-Guided Pruner Evolution (PGPE) subsystem; declares the five submodules and re-exports the core Bayesian lifecycle types (PrecisionVector, PrecisionPolicy, SurpriseComputer, PosteriorEvidence, PosteriorGuidedPruner).
nodes.languageNotes: Rust module root using `pub mod` declarations plus `pub use` re-exports — typical crate-internal barrel pattern.

nodes.name: policy.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the posterior policy decision logic — maps a per-arm precision state, KL surprise, and optional peer precision into one of five LifecycleActions (Explore, Patch, Split, Compress, Retire) using a threshold-driven precedence cascade.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines a `LifecycleAction` enum, a `PrecisionPolicyConfig` of ten threshold fields, and a `PrecisionPolicy` struct whose `decide` method uses ordered short-circuit guards to pick the first matching action.

nodes.name: precision.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `PrecisionVector` — a BAKE-style sequential Bayesian updater that tracks per-dimension precision/mean, alpha/beta counts, and per-failure-mode tallies, plus derived queries (success probability, divergence, depletion, repeated-failure detection).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses fixed-size pre-allocated arrays for zero-allocation hot-path updates; failure modes are stored as `u8` counts indexed via `FailureMode::as_index`.

nodes.name: surprise.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `SurpriseComputer` — a sigmoid-gated KL-divergence surprise calculator that floors small divergences and weights surprise by average precision before returning a value used by the policy layer to trigger lifecycle actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Numerically stable sigmoid branches on the sign of x (uses 1/(1+exp(-x)) for x>=0, exp(x)/(1+exp(x)) for x<0) to avoid overflow.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the structured evidence vocabulary used by the posterior layer — `PosteriorEvidence` record plus `EvidenceOutcome`, `EvidenceContext`, `FailureMode`, `EvalBucket`, and `LatencyBucket` enums, each with an `as_index` mapping for vector slot assignment.
nodes.languageNotes: Each categorizing enum implements `as_index()` so evidence can be slotted into fixed precision sub-vectors without hashing.

nodes.name: wrapper.rs
nodes.summary:
Implements `PosteriorGuidedPruner

` — a decorator wrapping any `ScreeningPruner` with per-arm Bayesian precision tracking, evidence recording, lifecycle decisions, and a surprise-modulated relevance signal that promotes exploration of uncertain arms.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic over `P: ScreeningPruner`; the `relevance()` method blends the inner pruner's domain signal with a sigmoid exploration bonus and a precision-derived confidence multiplier, then clamps to [0,1].

nodes.name: LifecycleAction
nodes.summary: Enum of the five lifecycle actions a posterior-tracked arm can take: Explore (insufficient evidence), Patch (repeated failures with surprise), Split (divergence from peer), Compress (high precision), Retire (failure-dominant).

nodes.name: PrecisionPolicyConfig
nodes.summary: Threshold configuration for the precision policy — ten knobs covering patch surprise/failure counts, split divergence/observation minimums, compress precision thresholds, retire success-probability/beta floors, and surprise-beta/floor for the surprise computer.

nodes.name: PrecisionPolicy
nodes.summary: Stateful decision engine that wraps a `PrecisionPolicyConfig` and a `SurpriseComputer`, exposing `decide(precision, surprise_kl, peer_precision)` which evaluates a fixed-precedence cascade of lifecycle-action guards.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Core policy entry point — given a per-arm PrecisionVector, a KL surprise value, and an optional peer precision, returns the highest-priority applicable LifecycleAction by short-circuiting through Retire, Patch, Split, Compress, and Explore guards.

nodes.name: PrecisionVector
nodes.summary: BAKE-style Bayesian precision tracker — holds per-dimension precision and mean arrays, alpha/beta success/failure totals, total observation count, and per-failure-mode counts, with sequential update and a suite of derived statistical queries.

nodes.name: with_prior
nodes.summary: Constructs a PrecisionVector seeded with an explicit prior precision and mean vector instead of the default uniform prior — used when warm-starting from a previously trained or frozen posterior.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Sequential Bayesian update — given an outcome (success/failure), an observation vector, and an optional failure mode, adjusts per-dimension precision/mean via the precision-weighted delta rule, increments alpha/beta, and accumulates a clamped KL surprise into the failure-mode slot.
nodes.languageNotes: Precision-weighted mean update: `mean[i] += precision_ratio * (observation[i] - mean[i])`; KL surprise clamped to a u8-friendly range for storage.

nodes.name: max_failure_mode_count
nodes.summary: Returns the highest count across all failure-mode slots and the corresponding `FailureMode` variant — used by the policy layer to detect a dominant failure pattern triggering Patch or Retire.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `std::mem::transmute::<u8, FailureMode>` to reconstruct the enum variant from the slot index.

nodes.name: precision_divergence
nodes.summary: Computes the max absolute per-dimension precision difference between this vector and another — the divergence metric used by the Split lifecycle action to detect arms that have specialized away from their peer.

nodes.name: SurpriseComputer
nodes.summary: Sigmoid-gated KL surprise calculator — holds a beta scaling factor and a surprise floor; `compute_surprise` returns a precision-weighted sigmoid of (KL - floor), used by the policy to decide when surprising evidence should trigger a lifecycle action.

nodes.name: compute_surprise
nodes.summary: Combines a PrecisionVector's average precision with a KL divergence through the sigmoid surprise gate to produce a single scalar — higher precision amplifies surprise from the same KL, modeling that confident arms finding surprising evidence is more actionable.

nodes.name: PosteriorEvidence
nodes.summary: Structured evidence record passed to `record_structured_evidence` — carries task_id, outcome, context, failure_mode, eval bucket, and latency bucket, providing the full conditioning signal for the posterior update.

nodes.name: EvidenceOutcome
nodes.summary: Binary outcome enum (Success / Failure) used to route Bayesian updates to the alpha or beta counter and to gate the precision-weighted mean update direction.

nodes.name: EvidenceContext
nodes.summary: Domain context enum (Generic, Sudoku, Bomber, Go, Dungeon, Monopoly) identifying which game/task family an evidence sample came from — used to condition posterior updates per domain.

nodes.name: FailureMode
nodes.summary: Taxonomy of seven failure modes (FalseAccept, FalseReject, Timeout, FormatMismatch, BlankOutput, WrongValue, ContextConfusion) tracked per-arm to distinguish dominant failure patterns for Patch/Retire decisions.

nodes.name: EvalBucket
nodes.summary: Coarse bucketing of evaluation counts (Zero/Low/Medium/High/VeryHigh) via `from_count`, providing a discrete conditioning dimension for the observation vector without storing raw counts.

nodes.name: LatencyBucket
nodes.summary: Coarse bucketing of response latency (Instant/Fast/Medium/Slow/VerySlow) via `from_nanos`, used as a conditioning signal to distinguish fast-correct from slow-correct outcomes.

nodes.name: PosteriorGuidedPruner
nodes.summary: Generic decorator over any `ScreeningPruner` that maintains per-arm PrecisionVectors, a PrecisionPolicy, and reward/visit tallies; the integration surface between the inner domain pruner and the Bayesian posterior layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic `PosteriorGuidedPruner<P: ScreeningPruner>` — bounds the inner pruner by the `ScreeningPruner` trait from `katgpt_core`.

nodes.name: with_policy_config
nodes.summary: Constructor variant that accepts an explicit `PrecisionPolicyConfig` instead of the default — used when warm-starting the pruner with tuned lifecycle thresholds (e.g. from a frozen policy).

nodes.name: record_evidence
nodes.summary: Records a (arm, outcome, failure_mode, reward) observation — bounds-checks the arm, builds an observation vector from internal visit/reward state, and applies the sequential Bayesian update to that arm's PrecisionVector.

nodes.name: record_structured_evidence
nodes.summary: Accepts a fully structured `PosteriorEvidence` record plus an arm index, validates the arm, and delegates to `record_evidence` after unpacking the outcome and failure_mode fields.

nodes.name: lifecycle_action_with_peer
nodes.summary: Returns the LifecycleAction for an arm given an optional peer arm — reads the per-arm last_surprise and the peer's PrecisionVector, then delegates the decision to `PrecisionPolicy::decide`.

nodes.name: best_arm
nodes.summary: Returns the arm index with the strongest posterior — iterates per-arm PrecisionVectors, filters by a minimum observation count, and picks the highest success_probability, falling back to total observations as a tiebreaker.

nodes.name: build_observation
nodes.summary: Constructs the fixed-size observation vector passed to `PrecisionVector::update` — encodes per-arm visit ratio, normalized cross-arm observation distribution, and current alpha/beta as the conditioning features for the Bayesian update.

nodes.name: relevance
nodes.summary: Decorated relevance signal — takes the inner pruner's domain relevance for the token, scales it by a precision-derived confidence multiplier, adds a sigmoid exploration bonus for under-visited arms, and clamps to [0,1]; retired arms short-circuit to zero.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the classic explore/exploit blend: `relevance = clamp(domain * confidence + exploration_bonus, 0, 1)` where confidence scales with success probability and the bonus decays with visits.

nodes.name: coincidence_gate.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the CoincidenceGate — a theorem-backed cross-task transfer primitive that probes a known optimum x* from one simple objective against other simple objectives, achieving an exponential hit-rate lift over random sampling. Includes inline tests for boundary behavior and probe-transfer ranking.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust newtype-less struct with inherent methods; uses an injected Rng trait for deterministic probe sampling in tests.

nodes.name: complexity_prior.rs
nodes.summary: Core algorithmic-probability sampler for katgpt-pruners: defines the ComplexityProxy trait with five pluggable K-tilde estimators (RLE ratio, Shannon entropy, L1 norm, LZ4, Blake3 canonical length) and the CompressionPriorSampler that replaces uniform candidate sampling with per-candidate sigmoid(-alpha*K-tilde - beta)-weighted sampling (never softmax). Ships a latent variant operating on &[f32] via byte-quantization plus inline tests and an LCG used by tests.
nodes.languageNotes: Trait + five impls pattern; generic CompressionPriorSampler<K: ComplexityProxy> with Default; LatentCompressionPriorSampler is a newtype wrapper delegating to the byte-quantized inner sampler.

nodes.name: integration_bandit.rs
nodes.summary: KPriorBandit integration hook (feature `bandit_k_prior`): wraps a CompressionPriorSampler to score multi-armed bandit arms by their log algorithmic-probability prior, preferring low-complexity (high-prior) arms. Includes inline tests verifying delegation and arm ranking.
nodes.languageNotes: Feature-gated module compiled only under `bandit_k_prior`; thin wrapper over the generic CompressionPriorSampler.

nodes.name: integration_mcts.rs
nodes.summary: MCTS expansion priors (feature `mcts_k_prior`): defines the MctsExpansionPrior trait with UniformExpansion (flat log-prior of 0.0) and KPriorExpansion (algorithmic-probability-weighted via CompressionPriorSampler.log_prob) implementations for biasing Monte Carlo tree search toward low-complexity children.
nodes.languageNotes: Two trait impls on marker structs (UniformExpansion, KPriorExpansion) demonstrating the strategy pattern in Rust.

nodes.name: integration_spec.rs
nodes.summary: KPriorDrafter integration hook (feature `spec_k_prior`): reranks speculative-decoding drafts by adding each draft's log algorithmic-probability prior to its verifier score, boosting low-K (simple) drafts. Includes tests for rerank semantics and empty-draft edge cases.
nodes.languageNotes: In-place reranking mutates a borrowed scores slice; delegation to sampler.log_prob for the prior term.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel for the screening primitives of katgpt-pruners, re-exporting the CompressionPriorSampler family and CoincidenceGate plus three feature-gated integration hooks (MCTS, bandit, speculative decoding). Module docs record the open modelless-inference boundary (no HLA/functor/shard types — those live in riir-ai).
nodes.languageNotes: Each integration module is a zero-cost `pub mod` under a `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` gate so the entire module drops when the feature is off.

nodes.name: CoincidenceGate
nodes.summary: Cross-task transfer gate holding a simple-set size estimate; provides should_probe (decide whether to test x* against a new objective) and probe_transfer (sample objectives that x* hits within rank threshold r).

nodes.name: probe_transfer
nodes.summary: Given optimum x* and a list of objective functions, samples up to rank_threshold_r*2 objectives and returns those whose f2_k(x*) exceeds a random threshold — implementing the coincidence-transfer probe from Dingle-Hutter.

nodes.name: should_probe
nodes.summary: Decides whether a candidate objective's K-tilde is below the gate's simple-set size estimate, indicating it is simple enough to warrant a coincidence probe.

nodes.name: ComplexityProxy
nodes.summary: Trait abstraction over Kolmogorov-complexity estimators K-tilde(&[u8]) -> f32; implemented by RLE, Shannon entropy, L1, LZ4, and Blake3 canonical-length proxies and consumed by CompressionPriorSampler.

nodes.name: RleComplexity
nodes.summary: ComplexityProxy estimating K-tilde as the run-length-encoded length of the candidate bytes — a fast compression-ratio proxy for algorithmic complexity.

nodes.name: EntropyComplexity
nodes.summary: ComplexityProxy estimating K-tilde as the Shannon entropy (in bits) of the candidate byte distribution.

nodes.name: L1Complexity
nodes.summary: ComplexityProxy estimating K-tilde as the L1 norm (sum of byte values) of the candidate — a coarse magnitude-based complexity proxy.

nodes.name: Lz4Complexity
nodes.summary: ComplexityProxy estimating K-tilde via the LZ4 compressed length of the candidate bytes; implements Default for use as the standard compression proxy.

nodes.name: Blake3CanonicalLengthComplexity
nodes.summary: ComplexityProxy estimating K-tilde via a Blake3-derived canonical encoding length — a collision-resistant hashing proxy used for canonical-form complexity comparison.

nodes.name: CompressionPriorSampler
nodes.summary: Generic algorithmic-probability sampler<K: ComplexityProxy> with alpha/beta temperatures; provides log_prob, sample_ix (sigmoid-weighted categorical sampling), and top_k selection. Default never worse than uniform.

nodes.name: LatentCompressionPriorSampler
nodes.summary: Newtype wrapping CompressionPriorSampler to operate on &[f32] latent vectors via byte-quantization (quantize_latent); exposes log_prob_latent, sample_ix_latent, and top_k_latent mirroring the byte-domain API.

nodes.name: rle_compressed_len
nodes.summary: Computes the run-length-encoded byte length of a candidate slice using div_ceil packed run counters — used by RleComplexity.

nodes.name: shannon_entropy_bits
nodes.summary: Computes the Shannon entropy (in bits) of the empirical byte distribution of a slice — used by EntropyComplexity.

nodes.name: sigmoid
nodes.summary: Numerically stable logistic sigmoid 1/(1+e^{-x}) used to turn per-candidate log-priors into sampling probabilities (per-candidate sigmoid, never softmax).

nodes.name: log_prob
nodes.summary: Returns the log algorithmic-probability prior of a candidate as -(alpha*K-tilde(candidate) + beta) — the per-candidate scoring function consumed by all three integration hooks (bandit, MCTS, speculative).

nodes.name: sample_ix
nodes.summary: Samples a candidate index from the slice with probability proportional to sigmoid(log_prob(candidate)), using an injected Rng; uses black_box to prevent the optimizer from eliding the sampling loop in benchmarks.

nodes.name: top_k
nodes.summary: Selects the top-k candidate indices ranked by log_prob (lowest complexity first), writing them into a caller-provided output slice and returning the number filled.

nodes.name: quantize_latent
nodes.summary: Quantizes a &[f32] latent vector into bytes by min-max scaling to [0, 255] with finite-span guards, enabling byte-domain complexity proxies to operate on latent vectors.

nodes.name: sample_ix_latent
nodes.summary: Latent variant of sample_ix: quantizes each &[f32] candidate to bytes via quantize_latent, then samples by sigmoid(log_prob) over the byte encoding.

nodes.name: top_k_latent
nodes.summary: Latent variant of top_k: quantizes &[f32] candidates to bytes and returns the k lowest-complexity indices via the inner sampler's log_prob.

nodes.name: KPriorBandit
nodes.summary: Bandit wrapper around a CompressionPriorSampler exposing arm_log_prior(arm_bytes) — the log algorithmic-probability prior of an arm, used to bias arm selection toward low-complexity arms.

nodes.name: arm_log_prior
nodes.summary: Returns the log algorithmic-probability prior of a bandit arm by delegating to the wrapped CompressionPriorSampler.log_prob on the arm's byte sequence.

nodes.name: MctsExpansionPrior
nodes.summary: Trait abstraction over MCTS expansion priors: log_prior(sampler, candidate) -> f32 returns the log-prior weight applied to a child node during expansion. Implemented by UniformExpansion and KPriorExpansion.

nodes.name: UniformExpansion
nodes.summary: MctsExpansionPrior implementation returning a flat log-prior of 0.0 for any candidate, preserving standard uniform MCTS expansion as a baseline.

nodes.name: KPriorExpansion
nodes.summary: MctsExpansionPrior implementation delegating to CompressionPriorSampler.log_prob to bias MCTS expansion toward children with low algorithmic complexity (high prior).

nodes.name: log_prior
nodes.summary: KPriorExpansion::log_prior — delegates to CompressionPriorSampler.log_prob(candidate) to score an MCTS child by its algorithmic-probability prior; the UniformExpansion impl returns 0.0.

nodes.name: KPriorDrafter
nodes.summary: Speculative-decoding drafter wrapping a CompressionPriorSampler; reranks draft candidates by adding each draft's log algorithmic-probability prior to its verifier score in place, boosting low-K (simple) drafts.

nodes.name: rerank
nodes.summary: Adds sampler.log_prob(draft_bytes) to each entry of a borrowed scores slice, reranking speculative-decoding drafts in place by their combined verifier score and algorithmic-probability prior.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for katgpt-sleep, the sleep-time compute subsystem. Declares all internal modules (types, predictability, anticipator, consume, cost_model) and re-exports their public APIs as the crate surface.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust lib.rs serving as the crate root with module declarations and pub-use re-exports.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Core data model for sleep-time anticipation: AnticipatedQueryDir (committed forecast direction with BLAKE3 hash), AnticipatedSlot (direction + precomputed output + predictability), and AnticipatedQuerySet (committed const-generic slot collection).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses const generics (e.g. AnticipatedQuerySet<const N: usize, const M: usize>) and BLAKE3 hashing for tamper-evident commitment of precomputed directions.

nodes.name: predictability.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the PredictabilityScorer trait and its DotPredictabilityScorer implementation, which scores how predictable a context is for a forecast direction via SIMD dot product passed through a sigmoid gate with alpha/beta shaping parameters.
nodes.languageNotes: Trait + concrete impl pattern; predictability computed as fast_sigmoid(alpha * simd_dot_f32(c, dir) + beta).

nodes.name: anticipator.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the SleepTimeAnticipator that, given a context and a set of forecast directions, scores each via a PredictabilityScorer and emits a committed AnticipatedQuerySet of slots ranked by predictability within a token/time budget.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the SleepTimeComputeOp trait (with IdentityFunctorOp as the no-op default) to decouple the anticipation loop from the actual sleep-time compute kernel.

nodes.name: consume.rs
nodes.summary: Wake-time consumption layer: given a query and a precomputed AnticipatedQuerySet, find_best_match locates the nearest cached slot via SIMD cosine/distance, and consume / consume_gate sigmoid-blend the precomputed output with a fresh think based on predictability.
nodes.languageNotes: ConsumeMatchMode enum selects between Direction (cosine) and Precomputed (cached slot) match strategies; blend uses fast_sigmoid for smooth rather than hard switching.

nodes.name: cost_model.rs
nodes.summary: Amortization cost model for sleep-time precomputation: given sleep cost, number of consumers, and a sigmoid gate hit rate e_gate, computes expected wake cost per consumer, total cost, break-even consumer count, and a should_pre_compute decision.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-stateless math model parameterized by (t, b_max, tau, beta); e_gate is clamped to [0,1] before all formulae to keep them numerically stable.

nodes.name: AnticipatedQueryDir
nodes.summary: A forecast direction vector paired with a version tag and a BLAKE3 commitment hash, so any tampering with the direction bytes is detectable on verify_commitment.

nodes.name: AnticipatedSlot
nodes.summary: A single precomputed slot bundling an AnticipatedQueryDir, its precomputed output, and the predictability score that ranked it.

nodes.name: AnticipatedQuerySet
nodes.summary: Const-generic collection of N slots (up to M capacity) with a version tag and BLAKE3 commitment, providing commit_slots and verify_commitment for tamper-evident batch integrity.
nodes.languageNotes: Const generics <const N: usize, const M: usize> let the set be stack-allocated with a fixed capacity known at compile time.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs an AnticipatedQueryDir from a direction vector, computing its initial BLAKE3 commitment via commit_direction.

nodes.name: with_version
nodes.summary: Constructs an AnticipatedQueryDir with an explicit version tag while preserving the commitment scheme over the supplied direction.

nodes.name: commit_direction
nodes.summary: Hashes the direction's little-endian float bytes through BLAKE3 to produce the commitment digest stored on the AnticipatedQueryDir.

nodes.name: commit_slots
nodes.summary: Hashes all slot directions, precomputed outputs, and predictability scores (little-endian) through BLAKE3 to produce the AnticipatedQuerySet's batch commitment digest.

nodes.name: PredictabilityScorer
nodes.summary: Trait abstraction for scoring how predictable a context c is for a forecast direction dir, returning a value in the unit interval.

nodes.name: DotPredictabilityScorer
nodes.summary: Concrete PredictabilityScorer that computes fast_sigmoid(alpha * simd_dot_f32(c, dir) + beta), with alpha/beta parameters to shift the gate threshold toward or against precomputation.

nodes.name: predictability
nodes.summary: Scores predictability as fast_sigmoid(alpha * simd_dot_f32(c, dir) + beta), yielding a unit-interval confidence used by the anticipator and consume blend.

nodes.name: SleepTimeComputeOp
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting the sleep-time compute kernel; given a context, direction, budget, and scratch buffer, sleep_compute produces the precomputed output that will be cached in an AnticipatedSlot.

nodes.name: SleepTimeAnticipator
nodes.summary: Drives the sleep-time anticipation loop: holds a SleepTimeComputeOp, a PredictabilityScorer, per-direction budgets, and sigmoid shaping parameters tau/beta that together produce a committed AnticipatedQuerySet.

nodes.name: anticipate
nodes.summary: For each forecast direction, runs the compute op and predictability scorer, ranks slots by score, and commits the top-k into an AnticipatedQuerySet returned to the caller.

nodes.name: sleep_compute
nodes.summary: IdentityFunctorOp's sleep_compute implementation: a no-op kernel that returns the input direction untouched, used as a default and in tests where real compute is not exercised.

nodes.name: ConsumeMatchMode
nodes.summary: Enum selecting the slot-matching strategy: Direction matches by cosine similarity to the query direction, while Precomputed matches against cached precomputed outputs.

nodes.name: find_best_match
nodes.summary: Scans the precomputed slots and returns the index and similarity of the best match for the query, using SIMD cosine (Direction mode) or SIMD squared distance (Precomputed mode).

nodes.name: consume_with_match_mode
nodes.summary: Core wake-time consume: finds the best precomputed slot via the chosen match mode, then sigmoid-blends (gated by tau/beta) the cached output with a fresh_think callback based on predictability.

nodes.name: consume
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper around consume_with_match_mode using the default Direction match strategy, blending the precomputed slot with the fresh_think callback.

nodes.name: consume_gate_with_match_mode
nodes.summary: Returns only the sigmoid gate value (in [0,1]) for the best-matched slot under the chosen match mode, without invoking the fresh_think callback.

nodes.name: consume_gate
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper around consume_gate_with_match_mode using the default Direction match strategy; returns the gate scalar used to blend cached vs fresh outputs.

nodes.name: AmortizationCostModel
nodes.summary: Stateless cost-model parameterized by (t, b_max, tau, beta) that derives expected wake cost per consumer, total amortized cost, break-even consumer count, and a should_pre_compute policy from sleep cost and hit rate.

nodes.name: should_pre_compute
nodes.summary: Decision rule returning true when the clamped hit rate e_gate exceeds the configured tau threshold, indicating sleep-time precomputation is worth the cost.

nodes.name: amortization_factor
nodes.summary: Computes the ratio of total amortized cost over sleep cost, used to quantify how many consumers are needed to make precomputation pay off.

nodes.name: break_even_n
nodes.summary: Solves for the minimum number of consumers required for sleep-time precomputation to break even with on-demand wake-time compute, given the clamped hit rate.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the katgpt-band cluster (Plan 265 / arXiv:2605.12733) that re-exports four feature-gated modules: band_conditioner (foundation), bckvss (KV segment selector), collider_pruner (DDTree constraint), and adaptive_cot_stopper (CoT stopping).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses #[cfg(feature = ...)] gating so downstream crates can depend on only the substrate they need; the four modules share paper origin (Plan 265) and the conditional-independence-test substrate.

nodes.name: adaptive_cot_stopper.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the theory-backed adaptive chain-of-thought stopping criterion (paper Algorithm 1 + Theorem 1): stop thinking once no unresolved task collider segment pair remains, with a sigmoid-bounded residual structure-uncertainty score.
nodes.languageNotes: Standalone (no crate:: deps); uses katgpt_core::sigmoid. should_continue and uncertainty are O(1) hot paths over a HashSet of unresolved segment pairs.

nodes.name: band_conditioner.rs
nodes.summary: Foundation module of the cluster: defines the 4-element band conditioning set Z_band(k,v,i) from paper Theorem 1 and two conditional-independence tests (Fisher-z partial correlation and InfoNCE bound) plus CiTestTier/ComputeTarget routing enums.
nodes.languageNotes: Sink of the cluster's internal dep graph; fixed-size [u32; 4] storage avoids allocation on the hot path. Both CI tests return sigmoid-bounded scores in [0,1] (project rule: never softmax).

nodes.name: bckvss.rs
nodes.summary: Fusion A — Band-Conditioned KV Segment Selector that applies paper Theorem 1 to KV-cache retention: given a query as task collider g_i, retains exactly those KV segments whose representatives remain conditionally dependent, achieving O(N) instead of O(N^2) via segment homogeneity.
nodes.languageNotes: Zero-alloc hot path using caller-provided scratch; SIMD cosine similarity via katgpt_core::simd::simd_dot_f32. Includes SyntheticScm AR(1) benchmark generator with fastrand.

nodes.name: collider_pruner.rs
nodes.summary: Fusion C — Collider-Consistency ConstraintPruner (CCCP) for DDTree branch pruning: a drafted token branch is valid iff extending it preserves at least one tracked task collider's conditional dependence; dead branches are rejected. Implements katgpt_core::{ConstraintPruner, PreservationScorer}.
nodes.languageNotes: Composes with katgpt_core::NoPruner: when active_task_colliders is empty, behavior is identical to NoPruner (< 5ns overhead, GOAT G9). Batched hidden-state path avoids per-candidate recompute.

nodes.name: AdaptiveCoTStopper
nodes.summary: Tracks the set of unresolved segment pairs (k,v) and exposes should_continue / uncertainty / resolve / progress; thinking continues while any pair remains and stops once the residual structure-uncertainty (sigmoid in unresolved count) drops below tau.

nodes.name: uncertainty
nodes.summary: O(1) sigmoid-bounded residual structure uncertainty in [0,1]: sigma(-lambda * unresolved_count), decreasing as more task colliders are resolved.

nodes.name: from_segment_count
nodes.summary: Convenience constructor that seeds unresolved_pairs with all (k,v) pairs for k<v over n_segments segments, giving a step bound of O(|U_0|).

nodes.name: BandConditioningSet
nodes.summary: Fixed-size ([u32;4] + count + task) representation of the paper's 4-element band conditioning set Z_band(k,v,i), with 1-indexed public API matching paper notation and allocation-free hot path.

nodes.name: CiTestTier
nodes.summary: Enum (Hot, Warm, Cold, Freeze) classifying CI-test computational cost tiers with a for_query constructor that picks a tier from the number of new CoT steps.

nodes.name: ComputeTarget
nodes.summary: Enum (Cpu, Simd, Gpu, Ane, Plasma) of compute backends for CI-test batches with a for_ci_test_batch routing constructor used by both bckvss and collider_pruner.

nodes.name: from_segments
nodes.summary: Builds the band conditioning set Z_band(k,v,i) for segments S_k, S_v with task i, segment length L>=2, and total horizon T, omitting out-of-range indices and returning 1-indexed state positions to match paper notation.

nodes.name: conditional_dependence_fisher_z
nodes.summary: Classical Fisher z-test on partial correlation: returns a sigmoid-bounded score in [0,1] where >0.5 indicates conditional dependence rejection at the configured alpha; fast path requiring approximate Gaussianity of residuals.

nodes.name: partial_correlation
nodes.summary: Computes the partial correlation r(x,y | Z) by projecting x and y orthogonal to the conditioning columns Z via project_out, returning the residual Pearson correlation; the core primitive behind the Fisher-z CI test.

nodes.name: project_out
nodes.summary: Orthogonalizes vector v against the columns in cols (least-squares residual projection), the workhorse for partial-correlation computation.

nodes.name: pearson_r
nodes.summary: Standard Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient over two slices with mean-centering; returns NaN-safe 0 when variance is degenerate.

nodes.name: inverse_normal_cdf_two_sided
nodes.summary: Inverse normal CDF (z-quantile) for a two-sided test at significance alpha, used by CiTestResult::rejects_at to convert alpha to the z-stat threshold.

nodes.name: conditional_dependence_infonce
nodes.summary: InfoNCE bound on conditional mutual information (paper Appendix C high-dimensional surrogate): requires a critic closure that a modelless engine can satisfy with a frozen pretrained encoder, returning a sigmoid-bounded score in [0,1].

nodes.name: KvSegment
nodes.summary: One retained KV-cache segment with token_range [start,end), flattened keys (seg_len * d_k), and flattened values (seg_len * d_v); exposes seg_len/d_k/d_v dimensions plus representative_key/representative_value accessors for the segment-homogeneity shortcut.

nodes.name: SegmentSelector
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting KV-segment retention (SRP: retention is distinct from katgpt_core::ConstraintPruner's token-structure validation); implemented by BandConditionerSelector.

nodes.name: BandConditionerSelectorConfig
nodes.summary: Builder-style config (segment_len, alpha, reject_threshold) with Default and with_*chain methods for tuning the BandConditionerSelector.

nodes.name: BandConditionerSelector
nodes.summary: Paper-faithful SegmentSelector impl: scores each candidate segment pair via score_segment_pair, then retains segments passing the band-CI test using zero-alloc select_batch with caller-provided scratch.

nodes.name: SyntheticScm
nodes.summary: Synthetic structural causal model AR(1) data generator with task leakage, block-size control, subspace separation, segment chunking, and ground-truth relevance labels for benchmarking BCKVSS retention quality.

nodes.name: cosine_similarity
nodes.summary: SIMD-accelerated cosine similarity over two f32 slices (truncated to shorter length), returning 0.0 when either vector is all-zero to avoid divide-by-zero.

nodes.name: score_segment_pair
nodes.summary: Scores a candidate segment pair against an anchor using the band conditioning set and the Fisher-z CI test, returning a sigmoid-bounded relevance score in [0,1] that drives retention decisions.

nodes.name: select_batch
nodes.summary: Zero-alloc hot path: scans candidate KV segments under a budget using caller-provided scratch, returning the indices of segments that pass the band-CI test against the query.

nodes.name: generate_inner
nodes.summary: Core AR(1) synthetic generator for SyntheticScm: produces keys/values with task-conditioned cross-task leakage and optional subspace separation for benchmark construction.

nodes.name: matthews_corr
nodes.summary: Matthews correlation coefficient between binary ground-truth and predicted retention labels; the headline evaluation metric for BCKVSS retention quality on synthetic fixtures.

nodes.name: perplexity_proxy
nodes.summary: Computes a perplexity-like retention-quality proxy from a query and retained segment set using cosine-similarity log-likelihood aggregation; lower proxy = better retention.

nodes.name: ColliderConstraint
nodes.summary: Holds segment boundaries + active task colliders and implements ConstraintPruner: a drafted branch is valid iff collider_preservation_score stays above preserve_threshold for at least one tracked collider; fast-path returns true when no colliders are tracked.

nodes.name: ColliderPruner
nodes.summary: Local extension trait on ColliderConstraint for collider-specific batch operations with cached hidden states, documenting how CCCP composes with katgpt_core::ConstraintPruner.

nodes.name: InterleavedTaskBenchmark
nodes.summary: Benchmark fixture that generates interleaved multi-task sequences with task boundaries, per-boundary hidden states, and dead-branch detection for evaluating CCCP pruning decisions.

nodes.name: collider_preservation_score
nodes.summary: Scores whether extending the tree to (depth, cand_hidden) preserves at least one tracked task collider's conditional dependence, using the band conditioning set and Fisher-z test over parent and candidate hidden states; sigmoid-bounded result in [0,1].

nodes.name: batch_is_valid
nodes.summary: Batched ConstraintPruner::is_valid path: validates multiple candidate tokens at a single depth against parent_tokens, writing accept/reject into a caller-provided results slice to avoid per-candidate allocation.

nodes.name: batch_is_valid_with_hidden
nodes.summary: ColliderPruner trait method: batched validation using candidate hidden states (avoiding re-derivation), delegating to collider_preservation_score for each candidate.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Generates an InterleavedTaskBenchmark fixture with n_tasks interleaved across n_steps at the given segment length, producing boundary positions, boundary hidden states, and a task-at-token map for CCCP evaluation.

nodes.name: gap.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the PairedLossGap math — from_log_probs construction, mean_gap / mean_gap_for_class aggregates, and the SIMD-optimized filtered_mean hot path with the three paper filters (AllTokens / TopKNoCopy / CopyNOnly), plus the Proposition 1 annotate_with_class_bounds reporting API.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses unsafe set_len + indexed writes for LLVM-auto-vectorizable f32 subtracts; SIMD masked-sum via crate::simd primitives for the zero-alloc filtered aggregates.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for the paired_loss diagnostic — declares the four submodules and re-exports the public types and taggers; carries the paper distillation docs (Plan 335 / Research 319, Li & Merrill 2026).
nodes.languageNotes: Module-level doc distills arXiv:2606.20936; paired_loss is a modelless, zero-alloc A/B token-level loss-gap measurement primitive (NOT Super-GOAT).

nodes.name: tagger.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the pluggable TokenTagger trait and ships the CopyNGramTagger impl that marks positions completing a repeated n-gram (the paper's COPY_k feature) for tag-stratified aggregation.
nodes.languageNotes: CopyNGramTagger is O(L*n) per position with a naive prefix scan; a hash-based O(L) version is deferred to Phase 2 if it ever lands on a hot path.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: G1 correctness test suite for the paired loss gap diagnostic — synthetic fixtures with known per-token deltas covering from_log_probs invariants, per-class mean_gap, all three filtered aggregates, the CopyNGramTagger, and the Proposition 1 annotate_with_class_bounds report.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Core data types for the paired loss gap diagnostic — PairedLossGap struct, TokenClass enum, ClassSizeBound (Proposition 1 log|V_τ|), FilterKind enum (the three paper filters), FilterScratch for the SIMD hot path, and ClassGapRow / ClassGapReport for the per-class annotation report.
nodes.languageNotes: TokenClass is #[repr(u8)] with CopyN(u8) for a 2-byte layout that keeps an 8192-length class array in L1 (16 KiB) instead of L2.

nodes.name: from_log_probs
nodes.summary: Constructs the per-token gap trace Δ_i = ℓ_A[i] − ℓ_B[i] from two equal-length log-prob slices with a single Vec::with_capacity allocation; panics on length mismatch (caller bug).

nodes.name: mean_gap_for_class
nodes.summary: Computes the mean Δ over positions whose TokenClass equals a target using an unchecked, branchless single-pass accumulation (skip when class empty).

nodes.name: filtered_mean_with_scratch
nodes.summary: Zero-alloc dispatch for the three paper filters — AllTokens delegates to mean_gap, TopKNoCopy takes the branchless fast path, CopyNOnly routes through the masked SIMD path with a reusable scratch mask buffer.

nodes.name: masked_mean_simd
nodes.summary: Builds a u8 mask once into the scratch buffer from a TokenClass predicate, then runs simd_masked_sum_count_f32 for the masked mean — the shared SIMD hot-path backend for all filtered aggregates.

nodes.name: filtered_mean_topk_nocopy_scratch
nodes.summary: Implements the paper's TOP-K∩NO-COPY filter — fast path (k≥2) masks Content+Function for one SIMD pass; slow path (k=1) ranks the two open-class candidates and returns the higher-mean one.

nodes.name: class_sum_count
nodes.summary: Branchless single-pass helper returning (sum, count) of Δ_i over positions whose TokenClass equals a target; used by CopyNOnly and the k=1 ranking fallback.

nodes.name: annotate_with_class_bounds
nodes.summary: Cold-path reporting API — accumulates per-class (sum, count) into a HashMap, joins each class with its Proposition 1 ClassSizeBound, computes gap_to_bound_ratio, and returns a ClassGapReport sorted by ratio descending with NaN-aware ordering.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: CopyNGramTagger classifier — scans the visible prefix for an earlier non-overlapping occurrence of the n-gram ending at `position`, returning CopyN(n) on match and Other otherwise; n saturates at 255.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Returns a fixed &'static str display label for a TokenClass variant (CopyN renders as "CopyN", omitting the n) — centralizes display logic for pretty-printing and examples.

nodes.name: for_vocab_size
nodes.summary: Constructs a ClassSizeBound with log_v_tau = ln(v_tau); guards v_tau=0 (returns +inf bound) and v_tau=1 (returns 0, deterministic class) per the Proposition 1 closed-form.

nodes.name: TokenTagger
nodes.summary: Trait abstraction for per-position token classification — produces the &[TokenClass] array reused across all filter queries; consumer-replaceable (POS tagger, code tagger, game-state tagger).

nodes.name: CopyNGramTagger
nodes.summary: TokenTagger impl that marks positions completing a repeated n-gram of length n (paper's COPY_k feature, §4 Pattern iii); the only tagger shipped in-tree, richer taggers are consumer-side.

nodes.name: PairedLossGap
