nodes.summary: Per-token paired loss gap trace Δ_i = ℓ_A − ℓ_B — owns a single Vec<f32> allocated once by from_log_probs; all query methods are &self and zero-alloc (the impl block lives in gap.rs).

nodes.name: TokenClass
nodes.summary: 2-byte #[repr(u8)] enum tagging each position as Content / Function / Other / BracketOpen / BracketClose / CopyN(n) for tag-stratified aggregation (paper §3 + §4 Patterns i–iii).

nodes.name: ClassSizeBound
nodes.summary: Proposition 1 class-size bound DKL(p⋆_τ ‖ p_ϕ,τ) ≤ log|V_τ| — holds the closed-form log_v_tau constant used to annotate which classes have room for a richer (latent) feature map to help.

nodes.name: FilterKind
nodes.summary: Enum selecting the paper's three filtered aggregates — AllTokens (baseline), TopKNoCopy { k, max_ngram } (the ~2× amplification filter), and CopyNOnly { n } (isolates visible-prefix retrieval).

nodes.name: FilterScratch
nodes.summary: Reusable u8 mask buffer grown-on-demand that lets filtered_mean_with_scratch hit zero net heap allocation across repeated calls — the scratch space for the SIMD hot path.

nodes.name: ClassGapRow
nodes.summary: Per-class annotation row pairing observed mean_gap with the Proposition 1 ClassSizeBound and exposing gap_to_bound_ratio (how much of the theoretical ceiling the observed A/B gap has consumed).

nodes.name: ClassGapReport
nodes.summary: Cold-path per-class Proposition 1 report — holds ClassGapRow entries sorted by gap_to_bound_ratio descending (NaN-aware, NaN last); produced by annotate_with_class_bounds.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for the O(sqrt(N)) factored retrieval memory (Plan 408 / Research 387). Gated re-exports of the freeze (Phase 4) and episodic delta-rule (Phase 5) wrappers, plus the always-on types and kernel primitives, implementing only the inference-time factored retrieval half of the FwPKM paper.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses #[cfg(feature = ...)] to keep the BLAKE3/episodic machinery out of the leaf-clean retrieval primitive; documents a deliberate softmax-at-top-k exception to the project's global sigmoid-gate rule.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Phase 1 skeleton and core types for the factored retrieval memory: the ProductKeyMemory<SQRT_N, D_K, D_V> table with const-generic dims, the ScoreFn enum (Dot/Idw), PkEntry/PkQuery result records, and a deterministic SeededRng for reproducible table initialization.
nodes.languageNotes: Const generics (SQRT_N, D_K, D_V) push dimension validation to compile time; row accessors return contiguous &[f32] views over flat Box<[f32]> storage with no per-row allocation.

nodes.name: kernel.rs
nodes.summary: Phase 2 retrieval kernel: implements the 2*sqrt(N) + k^2 factored top-k pipeline (score_dot / score_idw over both codebooks, heapselect_top_k_desc per half, cartesian_top_k over the k*k product, softmax_normalize_into) plus PkmScratch scratch buffers and the query_into entry point on ProductKeyMemory.
nodes.languageNotes: Whole pipeline is stack-only / zero-alloc via pre-sized PkmScratch buffers; brute_force_top_k + jaccard test oracles verify heapselect+cartesian matches O(N) ground truth.

nodes.name: freeze.rs
nodes.summary: Phase 4 freeze/thaw wrapper: FrozenProductKeyMemory wraps the PKM table in Arc<RwLock<Option<Arc<Table>>>> with an AtomicU64 version and a BLAKE3 content commitment, so commit() swaps in a new committed snapshot while readers observe a stable, versioned, hash-verified view without torn reads.
nodes.languageNotes: Outer Arc + RwLock<Option<Arc<Table>>> pattern: clones share storage (cheap), commit replaces the inner Arc under the write lock, AtomicU64::fetch_add bumps the version outside the lock for wait-free version reads.

nodes.name: episodic.rs
nodes.summary: Phase 5 delta-rule write gate (F1 fusion: PKM x delta-Mem): PkmEpisodicStore layers a mutable working ProductKeyMemory on top of a FrozenProductKeyMemory slot, applying V[idx] += gate * (target - V[idx]) to the top-k value rows and publishing atomically via the freeze slot's commit; one non-iterated delta step keeps it modelless.
nodes.languageNotes: gate is clamped to [0,1] with NaN -> 0.0 so curiosity-suppressed writes become no-ops; audit counters (writes_total / writes_applied / gate_sum) expose the modelless-vs-trained boundary for sync audits.

nodes.name: ScoreFn
nodes.summary: Enum selecting the half-codebook scoring function (Dot or inverse-distance-weighted), with idw_default / idw_with_epsilon constructors that validate epsilon finiteness.

nodes.name: ProductKeyMemory
nodes.summary: The core const-generic factored key-value table: two sqrt(N)-row codebooks (keys_1, keys_2 of D_K/2-wide rows) plus an N-row value matrix (D_V-wide), exposing contiguous row/flat views and constructors from raw slices, random init, and centroids.
nodes.languageNotes: All dims are const generics so assert_dims can panic on mismatched slice lengths at construction only; thereafter row indexing is pure arithmetic over flat Box<[f32]> storage.

nodes.name: SeededRng
nodes.summary: Private splitmix64-style deterministic PRNG used by ProductKeyMemory::from_random to produce reproducible key/value tables from a u64 seed.

nodes.name: assert_dims
nodes.summary: Const-generic-aware runtime assertion that the keys_1, keys_2, and values slice lengths match SQRT_N * (D_K/2), SQRT_N * (D_K/2), and SQRT_N * SQRT_N * D_V respectively, panicking at construction on any mismatch.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a ProductKeyMemory from caller-supplied keys_1, keys_2, and values Box<[f32]> slices, validating dimensions via assert_dims before taking ownership.

nodes.name: from_random
nodes.summary: Builds a reproducible random ProductKeyMemory from a u64 seed using SeededRng, filling both codebooks and the value matrix with f32 values in a fixed range.

nodes.name: from_centroids
nodes.summary: Builds a ProductKeyMemory from caller-supplied centroid codebooks and value matrix, delegating dimension validation and storage to new().

nodes.name: PkmScratch
nodes.summary: Pre-sized scratch workspace (per-codebook score arrays + top-K index/score buffers) reused across query_into calls to keep the retrieval pipeline allocation-free on the hot path.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Zeroing constructor for PkmScratch that allocates the per-codebook score and top-K buffers sized to the table's const-generic SQRT_N and K.

nodes.name: score_dot
nodes.summary: Computes the dot-product similarity between a query half and a codebook half-row, used as the Dot scoring mode for factored retrieval.

nodes.name: score_idw
nodes.summary: Computes inverse-distance-weighted similarity (log of squared Euclidean distance plus epsilon) between a query half and a codebook half-row, biasing retrieval toward spatially closer centroids.

nodes.name: heapselect_top_k_desc
nodes.summary: Partial-selection algorithm that maintains a min-heap of the K highest scores over a sqrt(N)-length score slice, avoiding a full sort on the retrieval hot path.

nodes.name: cartesian_top_k
nodes.summary: Combines the two per-codebook top-K lists into the final top-k over their k*k Cartesian product (by summed score), maintaining a descending-order output buffer.
nodes.languageNotes: Bounded k*k candidate enumeration is what gives PKM its 2*sqrt(N) + k^2 cost characteristic versus O(N) dense attention.

nodes.name: query_into
nodes.summary: End-to-end factored retrieval entry point: splits the query into halves, scores both codebooks via score_half, heapselects top-K per half, combines via cartesian_top_k, and softmax-normalizes the k weights into the caller-supplied out buffer.

nodes.name: softmax_normalize_into
nodes.summary: Numerically stable in-place softmax over the top-k (index, weight) entries, normalizing the restricted candidate-set weights to sum to 1; the documented PKM-internal exception to the project's global sigmoid-gate rule.

nodes.name: FrozenProductKeyMemory
nodes.summary: Concurrency-safe freeze/thaw wrapper around a ProductKeyMemory: inner Arc<RwLock<Option<Arc<Table>>>> for snapshot reads plus an AtomicU64 version counter, enabling cheap Clone-shared readers and an atomic commit() that swaps in a new committed snapshot.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a FrozenProductKeyMemory from a table, wrapping it in an Arc<RwLock<Option<Arc<Table>>>> and initializing the AtomicU64 version to 0; the version-0 BLAKE3 commitment is computed lazily by current_commitment().

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Atomically installs a new committed table snapshot under the write lock, computes its BLAKE3 commitment, and bumps the AtomicU64 version outside the lock so subsequent readers observe a consistent (table, version) pair.

nodes.name: query_into
nodes.summary: Read-side retrieval entry: snapshots current() under the read lock and delegates query_into to the underlying ProductKeyMemory, so concurrent commits never produce a torn retrieval.

nodes.name: current_commitment
nodes.summary: Returns the BLAKE3 content commitment of the currently installed snapshot, computing it lazily on first access after a commit if needed; used by verify() and the sync audit boundary.

nodes.name: compute_commitment
nodes.summary: Private BLAKE3 hashing of the dimension-tagged key_1, key_2, and value byte streams (via bytemuck cast_slice<f32,u8>), producing a content-addressed commitment that distinguishes structurally identical tables from raw-slice hashes.
nodes.languageNotes: Tagging the hasher with table dimensions before the byte streams defeats a naive collision where different (SQRT_N, D_K, D_V) tables hash to the same flat-byte digest.

nodes.name: PkmEpisodicStore
nodes.summary: Const-generic episodic store combining a mutable working ProductKeyMemory (the write target) with a FrozenProductKeyMemory slot (the published, committed view), plus u64 audit counters for total/applied writes and a cumulative gate_sum for mean-gate telemetry.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs an episodic store pre-loaded with a table: the table becomes the mutable working copy and is cloned into the freeze slot at version 0, so readers see the initial snapshot immediately while writes mutate the working copy until publish.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Delta-rule write path: retrieves top-k for q via the working memory's query_into, then moves each top-k value row gate fraction toward target (V[idx] += gate * (target - V[idx])); gate is clamped to [0,1] with NaN -> 0.0 so suppressed writes are no-ops; one non-iterated step so it stays modelless.

nodes.name: write_weighted
nodes.summary: Weight-scaled variant of write: each top-k value row is moved gate * retrieval_weight fraction toward target, so higher-similarity slots receive proportionally larger updates than the uniform-gate write path.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for katgpt-sparse: a feature-gated barrel that re-exports the sparse task-vector family (SOPTV storage, SPLAT specialist projection, and adapter composition) extracted from katgpt-rs per Proposal 003 Phase 11.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses #[cfg(feature = ...)] gates so consumers pay only for the sparse storage they need (sparse_task_vector base, specialist_projection pulls katgpt-band).

nodes.name: sparse_compose.rs
nodes.summary: Implements adapter composition for SparseTaskVector via mask intersection (preserves overlap floor, mean eta) and union (additive superposition, sum eta), distilled from arXiv 2606.13657 §4.3. Backed by an extensive GOAT G9/G10 property + paper-parity test suite.
nodes.languageNotes: Both composers allocate only the output Vecs (sized exactly to the result); no intermediate buffers. The module's second half is an inline #[cfg(test)] property suite covering associativity, commutativity, and overlap-floor preservation.

nodes.name: sparse_task_vector.rs
nodes.summary: Foundation of the sparse cluster: the SparseTaskVector storage format (sorted mask + parallel deltas + eta scalar) for OPD-style weight deltas, with from_dense/from_parts constructors, zero-alloc apply/subtract, density-aware metrics, and a gauge-invariant compose. Distilled from arXiv 2606.13657 (Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates).
nodes.languageNotes: Storage uses parallel Vec<u32> mask + Vec<f32> deltas with shrink_to_fit after construction; compose_gauge_invariant is a 77-line merge-sort-style union with abs-magnitude truncation honoring per-vector eta weights.

nodes.name: specialist_projection.rs
nodes.summary: Fusion B SPLAT specialist projection: estimates Jacobian image support via finite-difference Jacobian-vector products, builds a SpecialistMask that reuses SparseTaskVector storage, projects hidden states in-place under a sparsity bound, and routes CPU/SIMD/Plasma backends by density. Implements Prop 2 + Theorem 2 of arXiv 2605.12733.
nodes.languageNotes: JacobianSupportEstimator writes support indices directly into a caller-pre-sized Vec<u32> (zero alloc inside the finite-difference loop); enforce_sparsity_bound_with_mag uses select_nth_unstable_by for O(n) top-k magnitude pruning.

nodes.name: compose_intersect
nodes.summary: Compose two sparse task vectors by mask intersection: keeps only coordinates active in both inputs, sums per-coordinate deltas, and sets eta to the mean of the two inputs'. The paper's primary composition operator (arXiv 2606.13657 §4.3, GOAT G10).

nodes.name: compose_union
nodes.summary: Compose two sparse task vectors by mask union: keeps coordinates active in either input, sums overlapping deltas, concatenates disjoint tails, and sets eta to the sum of the two inputs'. Used for additive task arithmetic where intersection is too aggressive.

nodes.name: SparseTaskVector
nodes.summary: Core storage type for sparse weight deltas: parallel sorted mask (Vec<u32>), deltas (Vec<f32>), shape, and scalar eta. Provides construction, zero-alloc apply/subtract/scale, density metrics, gauge-invariant compose, and a Debug impl. The foundation of the entire katgpt-sparse cluster.

nodes.name: from_dense
nodes.summary: Constructs a SparseTaskVector from a dense delta slice by dropping coordinates whose absolute value is at or below a threshold (default 1e-5 per paper §4.1), then shrink_to_fit-ing the mask and deltas storage.

nodes.name: from_parts
nodes.summary: Validating constructor that builds a SparseTaskVector from pre-extracted mask + deltas + eta. Enforces length-match, sorted-ascending mask, and in-range indices, returning a typed SparseTaskVectorError on violation. The constructor used by every other builder in the cluster.

nodes.name: relative_norm_vs
nodes.summary: Computes the relative Frobenius norm ‖delta‖ / ‖base‖ using a SIMD-accelerated sum-of-squares kernel from katgpt_core, yielding the 0.04–0.14% paper-bounded relative update size.

nodes.name: compose_gauge_invariant
nodes.summary: Self-contained gauge-invariant composition: merge-sorts the two masks, superposes deltas at overlapping coords weighted by each vector's eta field, and truncates the result by absolute magnitude. The composition primitive referenced by the parity test against full sequential apply.

nodes.name: JacobianSupportEstimator
nodes.summary: Zero-sized type exposing estimate/estimate_into, which approximate the Jacobian image support I(J_u) of a specialist map via central finite-difference Jacobian-vector products against a task embedding direction. Output is capped at d_hidden coordinates per paper Prop 2.

nodes.name: SpecialistMask
nodes.summary: Coordinate-sparse specialist mask wrapping a SparseTaskVector; provides from_support construction, density/nnz/dim accessors, in-place hidden-state projection (zeroing non-kept coordinates per row), and conversion back to the underlying SparseTaskVector.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.summary: Allocating convenience wrapper around estimate_into: estimates the Jacobian image support of a batch of hidden states against a task embedding and returns a freshly allocated sorted Vec<u32> of coordinate indices (capped at d_hidden).

nodes.name: estimate_into
nodes.summary: Zero-alloc core of JacobianSupportEstimator: writes finite-difference Jv magnitudes into a caller scratch buffer, ranks coordinates by magnitude, and emits the sorted support (truncated to d_hidden) into a caller-provided Vec. Inner loop performs no allocations.

nodes.name: from_support
nodes.summary: Builds a SpecialistMask from a coordinate support list and dense shape by delegating to SparseTaskVector::from_parts with unit deltas and eta=1.0, reusing the sparse storage format DRY.

nodes.name: project
nodes.summary: In-place specialist projection: zeros every hidden-state coordinate not present in the mask, row by row, producing h_specialist = h · M_sparse per Theorem 2. Assumes the mask is row-major sorted; falls back to identity-like behavior on out-of-range coordinates.

nodes.name: enforce_sparsity_bound_with_mag
nodes.summary: Enforces the paper's sparsity bound ‖I(J_û)‖ ≤ ‖I(Ju)‖ by keeping only the top-k coordinates by absolute magnitude using select_nth_unstable_by (O(n) partial sort), then re-sorting the survivors ascending to restore the mask invariant.

nodes.name: specialist_score
nodes.summary: Computes a sigmoid-bounded specialist score in [0,1] from the alignment between a SpecialistMask and a hidden state: measures how concentrated the hidden state's energy is on the mask's kept coordinates, then squashes via the shared katgpt_core::sigmoid.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for katgpt-validator, a two-tier inference-time syntax pruner (Tier 0 PartialParser DFA + Tier 1 SynPruner using syn::parse_str). Re-exports the public API from the three submodules.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust crate root using `mod` + `pub use` barrel pattern; documents the architecture in a top-level doc comment.

nodes.name: partial_parser.rs
nodes.summary: Tier 0 O(n) bracket-balancer DFA. Tracks paren/brace/bracket/angle nesting depths plus string/char/comment lexer state to reject clearly unbalanced generated code cheaply before invoking the expensive syn parser.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-rolled single-pass byte scanner over `code.as_bytes()`; resettable state machine designed for incremental re-validation during speculative decoding.

nodes.name: syn_pruner.rs
nodes.summary: Tier 1 syntax pruner wrapping syn::parse_str::<syn::Stmt> for accurate Rust validation. Implements the katgpt_core::ConstraintPruner trait (is_valid/propagate) and threads a Mutex<PartialParser> and scratch-token buffer for token-level re-validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses std::sync::Mutex to share PartialParser and scratch_tokens across threads; gated behind the `hoare_pruner` feature for the propagate impl.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Shared validation types: PruneResult struct, ErrorKind enum (None/UnbalancedBrackets/SynError), and CompilerFeedback with helpers to extract repair suggestions from compiler error messages and render context snippets.
nodes.languageNotes: Small enum + struct module exposing the Result/Feedback surface consumed by both pruner tiers.

nodes.name: PartialParser
nodes.summary: Resettable bracket-balancer state machine tracking four bracket depths (paren/brace/bracket/angle) and four lexer states (string/char/block-comment/line-comment). Default trait impl delegates to new().

nodes.name: is_valid
nodes.summary: Single-pass scan over the input bytes updating all depth/state counters; returns false when any bracket type is over-closed, accounting for string/char/comment escaping and generic angle-bracket heuristics.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a fresh PartialParser with all bracket depths zeroed and lexer states disabled.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Returns the parser to its initial state so a new incremental validation pass can begin without reallocating.

nodes.name: SynPruner
nodes.summary: Tier 1 pruner wrapping a tokenizer, a Mutex<PartialParser> for cheap Tier 0 checks, and a Mutex<Vec> scratch buffer for token-level re-validation. Implements katgpt_core::ConstraintPruner.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Two-tier entry point: runs the PartialParser DFA first, and only on success attempts syn::parse_str::<syn::Stmt>, mapping parse failures into ErrorKind::SynError feedback.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a SynPruner wrapping the given tokenizer, initializing the Mutex<PartialParser> and an empty scratch-token buffer.

nodes.name: is_valid_quick
nodes.summary: Cheap Tier 0-only check that delegates to PartialParser::is_valid without invoking the syn parser; used to fast-reject speculative tokens.

nodes.name: is_valid
nodes.summary: ConstraintPruner trait impl: appends a new token to the scratch buffer, decodes the accumulated token stream, and asks the PartialParser whether the resulting partial source is still structurally valid.

nodes.name: propagate
nodes.summary: ConstraintPruner trait impl (hoare_pruner feature): mirrors is_valid's token accumulation but additionally resets the parser and reports the resulting total bracket depth so callers can rank DDTree expansions by structural plausibility.

nodes.name: CompilerFeedback
nodes.summary: Carries an error message, the failing code slice, and an optional repair suggestion; knows how to mine a rustc-style diagnostic for a suggested replacement and render a context string for logging.

nodes.name: extract_suggestion
nodes.summary: Parses a compiler error message looking for a help/suggestion span and returns the extracted replacement string, if any.

nodes.name: to_context
nodes.summary: Builds a compact context string combining the error message and failing code for diagnostic logging.

nodes.name: ane.rs
nodes.summary: Apple Neural Engine inference backend that programmatically builds CoreML neural-network specs from in-memory TransformerWeights at runtime, serializes them via coreml-proto, and runs the lm_head projection on ANE with CPU fallback for the rest of the transformer forward pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds CoreML protobuf specs in Rust via prost-generated types from coreml_proto::proto; uses cfg(feature = "ane") gating in lib.rs.

nodes.name: gpu.rs
nodes.summary: Metal compute GPU backend that embeds MSL (Metal Shading Language) kernels for RMSNorm, matmul, attention, and MLP, uploads all transformer weights to GPU buffers during compile, and runs the full forward pass on-device with only the final logits copied back to CPU.
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds MSL kernel source as a const &str string and compiles pipelines at runtime via the metal crate; uses cfg(all(target_os = "macos", feature = "gpu_inference")) gating.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for katgpt-backend defining the InferenceBackend trait that decouples the generate loop from concrete compute providers, the default CpuBackend delegating to katgpt_forward::forward, and an auto_backend selector that picks ANE, GPU, or CPU based on availability and residency checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Conditionally re-exports AneBackend and GpuBackend behind macOS-only feature flags; sits above katgpt-forward / katgpt-transformer / katgpt-types leaves with zero circular deps.

nodes.name: AneBackend
nodes.summary: Apple Neural Engine backend implementing InferenceBackend by lazily compiling TransformerWeights into a CoreML model and executing the lm_head projection on ANE with CPU fallback until compilation completes.

nodes.name: build_linear_model_spec
nodes.summary: Constructs a CoreML InnerProduct layer spec for a single linear (matmul) projection from a named weight matrix, embedding the weight and bias into the protobuf WeightParams.

nodes.name: build_transformer_model_spec
nodes.summary: Assembles the full transformer forward-pass graph as a CoreML NeuralNetwork spec: embedding lookup, per-layer RMSNorm/QKV/attention/MLP blocks, and lm_head projection, wiring every weight from TransformerWeights into the protobuf model description ready for ANE compilation.

nodes.name: build_conv2d_linear_model_spec
nodes.summary: Builds a CoreML ConvolutionLayerParams spec expressing a linear projection as a 1x1 conv2d, used when ANE preferentially fuses matmuls into convolution kernels for residency.

nodes.name: nn_layer
nodes.summary: Wraps a LayerKind into a named NeuralNetworkLayer with input/output tensor names, the common envelope used by all higher-level spec builders.

nodes.name: multi_array_type
nodes.summary: Constructs a CoreML ArrayFeatureType (multi-array feature) of the given shape, used to declare tensor inputs and outputs on the model description.

nodes.name: run_lm_head_into
nodes.summary: Feeds the hidden state into the compiled CoreML model and reads the lm_head logits back into the provided output buffer, performing the ANE-side prediction step.

nodes.name: validate_residency
nodes.summary: Times a micro-prediction on the compiled CoreML model and compares against an ANE-residency latency threshold to detect silent CPU/GPU fallback by CoreML.

nodes.name: GpuBackend
nodes.summary: Metal-backed InferenceBackend implementation that owns a Metal device, command queue, precompiled compute pipelines, and resident weight buffers, running the entire transformer forward pass on GPU via dispatch of MSL kernels.

nodes.name: scalar_buffer
nodes.summary: Allocates a Metal buffer carrying a single scalar value (e.g. epsilon or sequence-position constant) for use as a shader uniform.

nodes.name: InferenceBackend
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting one token + position → logits forward pass plus runtime weight compilation hooks (compile, is_compiled, recompile_hint, reset), implemented by CpuBackend, GpuBackend, and AneBackend.

nodes.name: CpuBackend
nodes.summary: Default InferenceBackend that delegates the forward pass to katgpt_forward::forward, used as the always-available fallback when ANE/GPU compilation fails or is unavailable.

nodes.name: auto_backend
nodes.summary: Factory selecting the best available InferenceBackend for a given BackendKind and model path, probing GPU then ANE then falling back to CPU on unsupported platforms or failed residency.

nodes.name: try_ane_backend
nodes.summary: Constructs an AneBackend instance when the ane feature and macOS target are available, returning None on unsupported platforms so auto_backend can fall through to the next provider.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for katgpt-hla, re-exporting the pure HLA substrate — cache state structs from types.rs and zero-alloc streaming recurrence kernels from kernel.rs — as a standalone publishable leaf crate with no dependency on katgpt-core or the engine.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust crate root using `pub mod` + `pub use` re-exports to surface the substrate API; katgpt-core re-exports this crate as `katgpt_core::hla` for backwards compatibility.

nodes.name: kernel.rs
nodes.summary: Zero-alloc streaming recurrence kernels implementing symmetric second-order HLA and asymmetric AHLA attention, achieving O(1) per-token memory by replacing the growing KV cache with fixed-size sufficient-statistic updates; provides both per-head primitives and full-layer GQA-aware helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `unsafe get_unchecked` with `debug_assert!` safety contracts for hot inner loops, `#[inline]`/`#[inline(always)]` for SIMD auto-vectorization hints, and a documented cross-term update-ordering invariant to prevent look-ahead bias.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the constant-size O(d²) and O(d·dv) inference cache state structs for symmetric HLA, asymmetric AHLA, and Parallax variants, including GQA-aware per-layer and multi-layer caches with memory accounting.
nodes.languageNotes: Ten plain `Vec<f32>`-backed structs with `new`/`reset`/`memory_bytes` constructors; `HlaVariant` is an enum exposing `floats_per_q_head` / `layer_bytes` sizing helpers used by the memory-budget planner.

nodes.name: transpose_matvec_into
nodes.summary: Cache-friendly i-outer/j-inner transpose-matvec kernel (`out[j] = Σ_i vec[i] · mat[i*hd + j]`) hoisted from 6+ hand-rolled call sites; the inner `qᵀ · SK` / `qᵀ · PKV` primitive at the heart of every HLA readout and cross-term.

nodes.name: hla_state_update
nodes.summary: Streaming recurrence update for one symmetric HLA Q head: computes causal-correction cross-terms G,h from OLD CQV,mQ, then accumulates SK, CQV, and mQ with optional gamma decay — enforces the correctness-critical update ordering.

nodes.name: hla_per_head_update
nodes.summary: Per-Q-head symmetric HLA accumulator body extracted from hla_state_update; computes the kᵀ·CQV and kᵀ·mQ cross-terms and applies the rank-1 SK/CQV/mQ updates with SIMD outer-product accumulation.

nodes.name: hla_readout
nodes.summary: Unnormalized symmetric HLA readout: produces the per-head attention output by combining qᵀ·CQV with the causal-correction terms qᵀ·G and qᵀ·h, unrolled over the head dimension.

nodes.name: hla_denom
nodes.summary: Computes the symmetric HLA normalization denominator (qᵀ·mQ corrected by the qᵀ·h term) used by hla_readout_normalized to produce scale-stable outputs.

nodes.name: hla_readout_normalized
nodes.summary: Normalized symmetric HLA readout that divides the raw attention output by the causal-corrected denominator (guarded by an epsilon against near-zero denominators), fusing readout and normalization in one pass to avoid an extra temp allocation.

nodes.name: ahla_step
nodes.summary: Asymmetric HLA (AHLA) single-step update for one KV group + Q head: applies gamma decay, accumulates PKV += k·vᵀ and E += outer products, then emits the left-cascaded A·A·V attention output capturing second-order interactions at linear-attention cost.

nodes.name: hla_layer_update
nodes.summary: Full-layer symmetric HLA update: applies gamma decay to shared per-KV-group SK buffers once, then dispatches per-Q-head accumulation via hla_per_head_update using the correct GQA head-to-group mapping.

nodes.name: hla_layer_readout
nodes.summary: Full-layer symmetric HLA readout that gathers per-Q-head outputs into attn_out, delegating to hla_readout_normalized when normalization is enabled and falling back to the raw hla_readout otherwise.

nodes.name: ahla_per_head_step
nodes.summary: Per-Q-head AHLA step body extracted from ahla_layer_step: computes the r = qᵀ·PKV readout, accumulates the E outer-product state, and updates the n normalization mass for one head given pre-decayed shared KV-group buffers.

nodes.name: ahla_layer_step
nodes.summary: Full-layer AHLA forward step: phase 1 updates shared PKV/mK per KV group (avoiding GQA double-accumulation), phase 2 dispatches per-head ahla_per_head_step, and phase 3 optionally normalizes the output by the ahla_denom correction.

nodes.name: HlaQHeadState
nodes.summary: Per-Q-head state for symmetric second-order HLA holding the query-value cross moment (CQV), query mass (mQ), and the causal-correction numerator (G) and denominator (h); 3hd² + 2hd floats per head.

nodes.name: HlaLayerState
nodes.summary: Per-layer symmetric HLA state with GQA-aware layout: shared key second-moment SK per KV group and a vector of per-Q-head HlaQHeadState entries, exposing the head_idx → kv_group mapping.

nodes.name: MultiLayerHlaCache
nodes.summary: Top-level multi-layer symmetric HLA cache aggregating one HlaLayerState per transformer layer, with configurable gamma decay and epsilon; exposes memory accounting and reset for the whole stack.

nodes.name: AhlaQHeadState
nodes.summary: Per-Q-head state for asymmetric AHLA holding the outer-product accumulator E (hd × hd) and the normalization mass n (hd) used in the left-cascaded A·A·V readout.

nodes.name: AhlaLayerState
nodes.summary: Per-layer asymmetric AHLA state with shared key-value prefix (PKV) and key mass (mK) per KV group plus per-Q-head AhlaQHeadState entries, exposing the GQA head_idx → kv_group mapping.

nodes.name: MultiLayerAhlaCache
nodes.summary: Top-level multi-layer asymmetric AHLA cache aggregating one AhlaLayerState per transformer layer with configurable gamma decay and epsilon; smaller per-layer footprint than the symmetric variant.

nodes.name: HlaVariant
nodes.summary: Enum tagging the Symmetric vs Asymmetric HLA variant, exposing sizing helpers (floats_per_q_head, floats_per_kv_group, layer_bytes) used by the memory-budget planner to compare cache footprints.

nodes.name: ParallaxAhlaQHeadState
nodes.summary: Per-Q-head state for the Parallax AHLA variant tracking running weighted key/value means (weighted_k_mean, weighted_v_mean), weight_sum, and sigma_kv second-moment — a richer head state for parallax depth steering.

nodes.name: ParallaxAhlaLayerState
nodes.summary: Per-layer Parallax AHLA state holding a vector of ParallaxAhlaQHeadState entries; thin layer wrapper that exposes new/reset for the whole layer.

nodes.name: MultiLayerParallaxAhlaCache
nodes.summary: Top-level multi-layer cache aggregating ParallaxAhlaLayerState per transformer layer with gamma decay; exposes memory accounting and reset for the parallax depth-steering stack.

nodes.summary: Project X ∪ Y jointly to R³ via the top-3 eigenvectors of the joint covariance; returns false on PCA collapse (zero variance).

nodes.name: fundamental_cycle_basis
nodes.summary: Extract a fundamental cycle basis (paper Definition H.1) via BFS spanning forest: for each non-tree edge, the basis cycle is that edge plus the unique tree path between its endpoints.

nodes.name: gauss_linking_integral
nodes.summary: Midpoint-quadrature evaluation of the Gauss linking integral between two basis cycles with bbox-separation early-skip; rounded to the nearest integer to produce the witness linking number.

nodes.name: subdivide_cycle_soa
nodes.summary: Structure-of-arrays midpoint subdivision of a cycle into n_sub segments per edge, preparing the Segments bundle consumed by the Gauss integral quadrature loop.

nodes.name: generate_npc_brain_model.py
nodes.summary: CoreML ML Program generator (Plan 254 / Research 224) that fuses three NPC think-brain ops (sense ternary projection, emotion dot-product, zone dot-product) into an ANE-optimized .mlpackage using coremltools' mb.program public API, with optional palettization, ANE-placement verification, and a raw .bin weights exporter.
nodes.languageNotes: Constants mirror katgpt-core/src/sense/backend.rs (MAX_MODULES=6, HLA_DIM=8, MAX_DIRECTIONS=8); ternary weights are losslessly converted to f32 at model-generation time.

nodes.name: TernaryDir
nodes.summary: Python mirror of the Rust TernaryDir type, holding a ternary sign vector and a to_float_weights method that losslessly expands -1/0/+1 to float weights for CoreML consumption.

nodes.name: SenseModule
nodes.summary: Python mirror of the Rust SenseModule, bundling a per-module ternary direction list and a project_weight_matrix method that builds the (MAX_DIRECTIONS, HLA_DIM) sign projection matrix consumed by the sense op.

nodes.name: build_npc_brain_model
nodes.summary: Constructs the CoreML ML Program for the NPC brain via coremltools' Builder API: sense projection (diagonal ternary sign x HLA state -> sigmoid), emotion dot-product -> sigmoid, and zone dot-product -> sigmoid, then converts the program to an MLModel.

nodes.name: quantize_model
nodes.summary: Applies coremltools OpLinearQuantizer palettization (OptimizationConfig + LinearQuantizer) to the MLModel and returns the compiled quantized model.

nodes.name: verify_ane_placement
nodes.summary: Loads an MLComputePlan from the compiled model and walks every ml_program operation, classifying each as ANE/GPU/CPU placement and returning a summary dict with counts and per-op details for ANE-readiness verification.

nodes.name: export_weights_bin
nodes.summary: Serializes sense-module weight matrices, emotion direction, and zone direction to a raw little-endian .bin file with struct.pack, padding matrices to (MAX_DIRECTIONS, HLA_DIM) for fixed-offset Rust-side loading.

nodes.name: project_ternary_reference
nodes.summary: Computes a Python reference implementation of the ternary sense projection (sign-gated softmax over direction confidences) for cross-checking against the CoreML model output.

nodes.name: make_test_modules
nodes.summary: Constructs a small fixture set of TernaryDir/SenseModule instances plus canned emotion and zone direction vectors for smoke-testing the export and projection paths.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses args (--batch-size, --quantize, --verify-ane, --output-dir, --export-weights), builds the model, optionally quantizes and verifies ANE placement, saves the .mlpackage, exports weights, and runs the ternary-reference projection cross-check with a full status printout.

nodes.name: release.sh
nodes.summary: One-command release orchestrator for katgpt-core: triggers release-plz to open a release PR, merges it into develop (no squash), promotes develop to main (--no-ff), explicitly triggers the publish workflow on main, waits for cargo publish, and fast-forwards main back into develop; a --publish subcommand supports manual CI publish from main.
nodes.languageNotes: Guards on gh CLI availability and auth; requires the user to be on the develop branch for the full flow or main for --publish.

nodes.name: router_compute_target.rs
nodes.summary: Module-energy compute router (Plan 264 Phase 4 / Fusion D) extracted from inference_router.rs as a pure mechanical move, picking the most efficient compute backend (Plasma/Simd/Gpu/Ane) from a modelless FFN/Attn energy profile and QPS, distilled from arXiv 2606.13657 section 4.2 Table 3 and gated by the module_energy_route feature.
nodes.languageNotes: All items re-exported from inference_router to preserve the public API path katgpt::inference_router::{ComputeTarget, ModuleEnergyProfile, route_by_module_energy}; the routing logic is restructured as a QPS-band match with an inner ffn/attn branch per band so each path evaluates at most one comparison.

nodes.name: ModuleEnergyProfile
nodes.summary: Per-module energy profile of a weight delta or adapter (FFN/Attn/Embed/Other fractions), with a PAPER_AVERAGE const (0.78/0.16/0.04/0.02), a total() accessor, and an is_valid() invariant that the four fractions sum to 1.0 within 1e-3.

nodes.name: route_by_module_energy
nodes.summary: Modelless routing rule that picks the ComputeTarget for the observed FFN/Attn energy fractions and QPS band: FFN-heavy low QPS routes to Plasma, attention-heavy high QPS to GPU, cold-start low QPS to ANE, otherwise SIMD fallback; rule order is significant so FFN-heavy at cold QPS still picks Plasma.

nodes.name: SpeculativeVerifier
nodes.summary: pub trait SpeculativeVerifier: Send + Sync with a single speculate() method that runs one speculative decoding step end-to-end and returns accepted tokens (always >= 1, up to gamma+1 with bonus). Strategy swap point for SimulatedVerifier (DDTree path) and LeviathanVerifier (real p/q rejection sampling).

nodes.name: BtComparison
nodes.summary: Recorded Bradley-Terry comparison record (winner/loser indices into the candidate pool) consumed by bt_fit.

nodes.name: is_passable
nodes.summary: Grid helper: true iff (r,c) is in bounds and not a wall tile. Used by find_path / find_path_multifloor.

nodes.name: sigmoid
nodes.summary: Branch-stable standard sigmoid used for gating decisions (NOT softmax per project constraint).

nodes.name: entmax_1p5
nodes.summary: Compute entmax-1.5 sparse mapping (allocating wrapper around entmax_1p5_into); returns (probabilities, threshold tau).

nodes.name: select_segment_size

nodes.name: select_policy
nodes.summary: SegmentAutoRoute method: maps current QPS to a CheckpointPolicy tier (Lazy/Normal/Eager).

tour.title: Project Overview & GOAT Mandate
tour.description: Begin with the project README, the canonical statement of what katgpt-rs is: a GOAT-proved neuro-symbolic micro-Transformer built for modelless inference only — no training, no backprop at runtime. The Key Results table anchors the tour (29x TTFT speedup, 93.8% KV reduction, 7079x Sudoku compression, +177 Bomber score) and frames the modelless-first mandate that constrains every downstream crate. Read this first to load the project's vocabulary and success criteria before touching code.

tour.title: Workspace DAG & Root Aggregator
tour.description: The root Cargo.toml declares the 27-crate workspace organized as a three-tier DAG: shared leaves depending on katgpt-types, katgpt-core as the trait-and-kernel hub, and domain stacks depending on core. The root src/lib.rs is not a published library but the dev/examples aggregator that wires every domain crate into the transformer runtime via ForwardContext, plus the only permanently root-resident code: training glue, benchmarks, and the inference router. Understanding this manifest up front makes every later crate's position in the dependency graph obvious.

tour.title: Types & Modelless Substrate
tour.description: katgpt-types is the leaf every other crate depends on: the master Config struct (micro/game/draft/gemma2_2b/qwen_deltanet presets), XorShift64 RNG, SIMD kernels, ternary math, and LoRA adapters. Its barrel lib.rs re-exports the full type vocabulary consumed across the workspace. katgpt-tokenizer extends the substrate with modelless BPE, ToaST split-tree, and ConvexTok LP-optimal tokenizers. These two crates define the data vocabulary the rest of the tour will manipulate, so they come first in the dependency descent.

tour.title: Core Cognitive Trait Contracts
tour.description: katgpt-core/src/traits.rs is the single highest-fan-in non-root file (19 importers) and the contractual foundation of the workspace. It declares ConstraintPruner (depth-aware validity/manifold-score/filtering), ScreeningPruner (relevance scoring), SpeculativeGenerator (draft emission), GameState, RolloutPolicy, LeoHead, DominoPruner, CollapseDetector, and the rest of the trait zoo. The crate's lib.rs aggregates ~100 submodules of cognitive kernels on top of these contracts. Every domain crate you visit later is bound to these signatures, so reading them here is non-negotiable.
tour.languageLesson: Rust traits with default method bodies (e.g. propagate/manifold_score returning defaults) let pruners implement only the behavior they override — the same pattern the standard library uses for default trait implementations, and the reason a 262-file pruner crate can share one contract without boilerplate.

tour.title: Cognitive Substrate & Key-Result Kernels
tour.description: Step inside the cognitive substrate to see where the README's headline numbers are produced. mux_latent implements MUX-Latent zero-training context compression (the 29x TTFT / 93.8% KV-reduction result). cgsp (Constrained Gradient Search via Probing) provides the derivative-curiosity direction-solver primitives. induced_cwm bundles the commitment/belief/ISMCTS/tournament kernels for induced conditional working-memory play. These are pure, side-effect-free algorithms — the modelless mandate means each kernel is a frozen, read-only transformation over the shared Config types from Step 3.

tour.title: Attention Stack & Spectral Quantization
tour.description: The attention and spectral primitives layer over katgpt-core. katgpt-attn/chiaroscuro computes DCT-based spectral entropy that drives KV tau-gating; katgpt-spectral/spectral_kv_cache is the per-layer store that normalizes, rotates, quantizes, and variable-bit packs K/V tensors at write time. katgpt-attn-match/compact is the ICML-2026 attention-matching compaction pipeline (NNLS beta fit + Cholesky Cv fit) that produces the README's prefill-sequence reduction. Together these three files span the whole attention compression surface the memory layer will build on.

tour.title: Speculative Decoding & Progressive MCGS
tour.description: katgpt-speculative is the shared draft-and-verify substrate extracted from the runtime: DDTree, DFlash, and the Progressive MCGS (Monte Carlo Graph Search) module. The progressive_mcgs cluster (graph, operators, search, types) is the most tightly coupled in the whole workspace, reflecting that branch-aware graph search over primary tree edges versus cross-branch reference edges is one coherent algorithm. This is where speculative draft acceptance — the hot path gated by the pruners in Step 10 — is actually executed.

tour.title: DEC Verification & Two-Tier Syntax Pruning
tour.description: Verification sits beside drafting. katgpt-dec implements Discrete Exterior Calculus: an oriented CellComplex with CSR coboundary index (types.rs, the highest-fan-in file in this layer) and the exterior-derivative/codifferential/Hodge-Laplacian operators that the speculative verifier uses to score draft geometry. katgpt-validator is the inference-time syntax gate — a Tier-0 PartialParser DFA for fast rejection plus a Tier-1 SynPruner using syn::parse_str for exact syntax-checked acceptance. This pair turns every draft from Step 7 into a constraint-verified, acceptance-ready candidate.
tour.languageLesson: A CSR (Compressed Sparse Row) coboundary index stores variable-length topological adjacency in three flat arrays (offsets, neighbors, orientations), giving O(1) per-element neighbor iteration with cache-friendly contiguous storage — the same layout graph libraries use for sparse adjacency.

tour.title: Memory Hierarchy & KV Cache Codecs
tour.description: katgpt-kv aggregates the compression, compaction, projection-sharing, and segment-checkpoint backends for the KV memory hierarchy. katgpt-quant provides the actual quantization codecs: TurboQuant (random rotation + Lloyd-Max codebook + bit-packing, arXiv:2504.19874) and OCTOPUS (octahedral-triplet KV compression with the (b+1, b-1) bit split). These deliver the 93.8% KV memory reduction and the 64x-fewer rotation FMAs (hybrid OCT+PQ codec) claimed in the README, sitting directly under the attention layer from Step 6.

tour.title: Constraint & Screening Pruning
tour.description: katgpt-pruners is the workspace's largest crate (262 files) and the gating engine for speculative draft acceptance and compute routing. bandit.rs — the highest-fan-in file here (16 importers) — implements UCB1, epsilon-greedy, and Thompson Sampling BanditPruners that wrap any ScreeningPruner for DDTree exploration. game_state/mod.rs defines the abstract GameState trait and MCTS infrastructure that powers the Bomber (+177) and Sudoku (7079x) results. absorb-compress promotes stable low-Q arms into hard blocks, turning online bandit learning into compiled constraint structure.

tour.title: Latent Steering & Belief Sampling
tour.description: katgpt-micro-belief is the latent-state control substrate and the workspace's other tightly-coupled cluster. types.rs declares the MicroRecurrentBeliefState trait and the RecurrenceFamily enum (Attractor / LatentThought / DeltaRule). attractor.rs implements the primary sigmoid-gated recurrent belief kernel (Xavier-scaled weights, SIMD dot, stack scratch), and bom.rs implements the BoM (Belief-of-Many) sampler behind the +31.49pp arena win-rate result. This is the steering layer — where sigmoid-gated direction vectors actually reshape the latent stream produced by the layers above.

tour.title: Symbolic Reasoning, Proof & Claim Reliability
tour.description: The reasoning layer gives the model its symbolic guarantees. katgpt-ruliology enumerates FSM/CA/TM strategies with a bandit pruner and a Pareto-front WinMatrix. katgpt-claim pairs an L0-L3 evidence-ladder rubric (claim_rubric/types.rs) with the CLR (Claim-Level Reliability) sigmoid-projection vote runtime (clr/vote.rs), the runtime that turns trajectory claims into reliability-gated, clustered verdicts. katgpt-proof-cert/certificate.rs defines the ProofCertificate / ProofProperty / ProofResult domain types that carry GOAT-style proof-certificate chains. This is what makes the system neuro-symbolic rather than purely neural.

tour.title: Forward Composition, Backend & Self-Verification
tour.description: The tour closes at the top of the stack, where everything is composed and verified. katgpt-forward defines ForwardContext — the pre-allocated scratch plus delta-routing that sits above the transformer and pruners — with d2f_context.rs holding the KV/attention/per-block scratch for diffusion-LM decoding. katgpt-percepta/graph/types.rs is the expression/dimension computation-graph DSL and MILP layer scheduler that turns the whole pipeline into a single executable plan, and katgpt-backend defines the InferenceBackend trait that decouples the generate loop from the concrete CPU/GPU/ANE provider. Finally katgpt-core/renoise_ce.rs is the Re-noise cross-entropy self-verifier (Plan 406, DEFAULT-ON, 100pp over plurality in the README) — the operator-agnostic capstone that perturbs, re-resolves, and measures drift to accept or restart, closing the loop on the modelless inference mandate introduced in Step 1.
